To address these limitations, we formulate low-light crack segmentation as a degradation-aware, prompt-grounded structural defect segmentation problem and propose DROA-CLIPSeg, a parameter-efficient framework that adapts a frozen CLIPSeg vision language backbone using two lightweight modules. QKV Low-Rank Adaptation is injected into the Q/K/V projections of the vision and text encoders to improve crack-specific image text alignment without backbone fine-tuning. The proposed Domain Residual Orthogonal Adapter (DROA) decomposes intermediate features into a dominant crack-domain branch, which captures recurring low-light crack patterns, and an orthogonal residual branch, which preserves faint, thin, and fragmented evidence usually suppressed by noise, shadow, or over-smoothing. We also introduce CrackLingo-9K and CrackLingo-12K, text augmented versions of Crack9k and Crack12k with crack-aware prompts. Training only approximately 1.93 M parameters, corresponding to 1.3% of the full model, DROA-CLIPSeg outperforms 9 zero-shot and 4 fine-tuned vision language baselines on both splits, generalises zero-shot to MVTec AD across textures and defect morphologies, and is supported by extensive ablations. Our source code is publicly available at https://github.com/VShuklacode/DROA-CLIPSeg
authors: Vinita Shukla, Partibha Jangra, Vinayak Pathak, Praful Hambarde, Amit Shukla
bullets: Addresses low contrast, shadows, glare, stains, joints, and wet seams that impair conventional crack segmentation.
Uses QKV low-rank adaptation to improve crack-specific image–text alignment without fine-tuning the backbone.
Introduces a Domain Residual Orthogonal Adapter that separates dominant crack patterns from residual faint, thin, and fragmented evidence.
Provides CrackLingo-9K and CrackLingo-12K, prompt-augmented versions of existing crack datasets.
Reports better performance than 9 zero-shot and 4 fine-tuned vision-language baselines, with zero-shot generalization to MVTec AD; results are limited to the evaluated datasets and settings.
papers.selection_reason: Adapts CLIPSeg for low-light crack segmentation using parameter-efficient adapters (QKV Low-Rank Adaptation, DROA), fitting Multimodal Foundation Models and Efficient AI.
papers.title: DROA-CLIPSeg: Prompt-Guided Thin Crack Segmentation in Low-Light Conditions
papers.tldr: DROA-CLIPSeg enables thin pavement-crack segmentation in low-light imagery by adapting a frozen CLIPSeg model with lightweight, crack-aware modules that preserve faint structural evidence.

papers.abstract: Simulation provides a low-cost sandbox where embodied agents can attempt tasks, observe outcomes, and learn from experience. Running many diverse simulation environments concurrently can consume substantial CPU and GPU memory because independently constructed scenes duplicate resources that remain unchanged across instances. We present Patchwork, a resource-sharing system for domain-randomized simulation, built around the representation $E=T+\Delta$: a shared template contains common resources, and a patch records the mutations needed to construct a target environment. Patchwork separates randomization sampling from replay and selects reusable templates together with patches that preserve each target environment's intended configuration. Its layered runtime shares compiled model structure and immutable assets while keeping mutable parameters and simulation state private to each instance. We implement Patchwork on robosuite and MuJoCo and evaluate it on LIBERO-plus and RoboCasa365 workloads. At 32 replicas, shared-template execution reduces CPU RSS by 88-92% relative to process-per-environment execution. Controlled experiments show how sharing shifts memory growth toward template diversity and unique asset content rather than instance count, within the supported sharing boundaries.
authors: Zixu Hao, Weijun Wang, Xiangyu Li, Liang Mi, Hao Wu, Yunxin Liu, Ting Cao
bullets: Addresses duplicated CPU and GPU memory from independently constructed simulation scenes.
Represents each environment as a shared template plus a mutation patch: E = T + Δ.
Separates randomization sampling from replay and keeps mutable parameters and simulation state private.
Implemented with robosuite and MuJoCo, evaluated on LIBERO-plus and RoboCasa365 workloads.
At 32 replicas, reduces CPU RSS by 88–92%; memory growth depends more on template diversity and unique assets than replica count within supported boundaries.
papers.selection_reason: Resource-sharing system reducing memory for domain-randomized embodied simulation, a technically transferable efficiency contribution to AI training pipelines.
papers.title: Replicate What Varies: Resource Sharing for Domain-Randomized Embodied Simulation
papers.tldr: Patchwork reduces the memory cost of running many domain-randomized embodied simulations by sharing reusable resources while preserving per-environment changes and state.

papers.abstract: Megapixel visual synthesis with latent diffusion models requires operating far beyond the resolutions at which these models are typically trained. Cascade refinement is a leading strategy for this setting: it starts from a base image at a native resolution and progressively upsamples it to the target resolution through multiple refinement stages. Each stage typically performs a pixel-space resolution transition followed by latent-space denoising. While prior acceleration efforts mainly focus on reducing denoising cost, we identify a complementary and underexplored bottleneck: the repeated movement of representations through the VAE. We call these operations pixel-space transitions. In cascade pipelines, intermediate latents are often decoded to RGB, resized, and re-encoded before refinement, while final latents are decoded patch by patch with dense overlap to suppress boundary artifacts. We propose UltraFlash, a transition-efficient approach that accelerates these VAE-heavy operations. UltraFlash has two components. Latent Hyperloop replaces intermediate RGB round trips with a learned latent-space shortcut that approximates the decode-resize-encode transformation without repeated VAE decoding and encoding. Sparse Patch-based Decoding accelerates final reconstruction by addressing patch seams caused by inconsistent GroupNorm statistics and reusing cached statistics across patches, enabling sparse VAE decoding with much smaller overlap. Integrated into a state-of-the-art cascade baseline, UltraFlash reduces 4K generation latency by approximately 2x while improving image quality. These results show that optimizing pixel-space transitions can improve both efficiency and fidelity, offering an effective route toward fast, high-quality megapixel visual synthesis.
authors: Phuc Lai, Anh Nguyen, Phong Nguyen, Anh Tran
bullets: Targets an underexplored bottleneck in cascade refinement: repeated decoding, resizing, and re-encoding through the VAE.
Latent Hyperloop replaces intermediate RGB round trips with a learned latent-space approximation.
Sparse Patch-based Decoding reduces overlap between final reconstruction patches by reusing GroupNorm statistics, mitigating seams.
Integrated into a cascade baseline, UltraFlash approximately halves 4K generation latency and improves quality.
Focuses on VAE-heavy pixel-space transitions rather than only reducing denoising cost.
papers.selection_reason: Reduces latency of VAE-heavy cascade visual synthesis; efficiency contribution to generative pipelines.
papers.title: UltraFlash: Accelerating Megapixel Visual Synthesis
papers.tldr: UltraFlash accelerates 4K latent-diffusion image synthesis by reducing costly VAE-based resolution transitions while improving image quality.

papers.abstract: High-resolution remote sensing (RS) imagery provides fine spatial detail over large areas, making it essential for fine-grained scene understanding. Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation (RRSIS) aims to segment regions described by natural language, yet many existing methods rely on sequential alignment--fusion pipelines with limited joint modeling of cross-scale visual hierarchies and linguistic dependencies. Moreover, dense attention mechanisms struggle with the sparsity and wide spatial dispersion of RS targets, while current datasets offer limited structured evaluation of multi-target references, multi-hop relational reasoning, and multi-granularity descriptions, limiting both model development and evaluation. To address these challenges, we propose a Cross-Scale Sparse Attention Model (CSSAM), which aligns multiscale visual features with complex referring expressions through two key modules. The Cross-scale Modality-aligned Fusion Module (CMFM) performs unified cross-scale cross-modal fusion, while the Dynamic Multimodal Sparse Hybrid Attention (DMSHA) selectively attends to informative visual--textual tokens, reducing dense visual interactions. Furthermore, we introduce M$^{3}$RRSIS-D, a RRSIS dataset explicitly designed around three core reasoning dimensions: multi-target (M$^{1}$), reference-dependent multi-hop (M$^{2}$), and multi-granularity (M$^{3}$) expressions. Extensive experiments on M$^{3}$RRSIS-D and two public RRSIS benchmarks demonstrate that CSSAM achieves competitive performance across accuracy, fine-grained reasoning, and high-IoU localization metrics, validating its effectiveness for complex semantic reasoning in realistic RS scenarios. Code, dataset, and model weights will be released upon acceptance.
authors: Yuxi Li, Lu Si, Xia Liao, Yidong Shen, Zheng Wei, Jun Zhang, Xin Yuan
bullets: Targets the difficulty of segmenting spatially sparse, widely dispersed regions described by complex natural-language references.
Uses CMFM for unified cross-scale cross-modal fusion and DMSHA to selectively attend to informative visual–textual tokens.
Introduces M³RRSIS-D, covering multi-target, reference-dependent multi-hop, and multi-granularity expressions.
Experiments on the new dataset and two public benchmarks report competitive accuracy, fine-grained reasoning, and high-IoU localization.
Code, data, and model weights are planned for release upon acceptance.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes dynamic multimodal sparse attention to reduce dense visual interactions, fitting efficient attention.
papers.title: Cross-Scale Sparse Attention for Referring Segmentation in Remote Sensing
papers.tldr: CSSAM improves referring segmentation in remote-sensing imagery by jointly fusing multiscale vision and language features with sparse attention, supported by a new reasoning-focused dataset.

papers.abstract: Image tokenizers convert pixels into compact latent sequences for efficient generative modeling. Most approaches arrange latents on a downsampled two-dimensional grid, tying sequence length to image resolution. We compare two variable-length strategies: computationally efficient patch-derived tokens, which inherit explicit spatial organization, and more demanding register tokens, which have no predefined spatial layout. Our reconstruction results reveal that patch-derived tokens perform substantially better under extreme compression, whereas register tokens achieve slightly better reconstruction quality at intermediate budgets. At high token budgets, both approaches achieve similar reconstruction quality. For downstream generative tasks, register tokens outperform patch-derived tokens. Adding representation alignment with external pretrained visual encoders substantially improves the generative performance of patch-derived tokens, allowing them to match or outperform register tokens depending on the token budget. We further find that both approaches learn spatially localized representations. Patch-derived tokens largely retain their explicitly imposed spatial organization, while register tokens develop an implicit two-dimensional spatial structure despite having no predefined layout. Representation alignment reduces this spatial organizational constraint, enabling individual tokens to exert a stronger non-local influence.
authors: Philipp Schenkel, Tobias Sch\"urmann, Omer Sahin Tas
bullets: Compares variable-length patch-derived tokens with layout-free register tokens for image tokenization.
Patch-derived tokens are substantially better at extreme compression; register tokens are slightly better at intermediate budgets, and both converge at high budgets.
Register tokens outperform patch-derived tokens in downstream generative tasks without additional alignment.
Aligning representations with pretrained visual encoders improves patch-derived generative performance, sometimes matching or surpassing register tokens.
Both token types develop spatially localized representations; alignment weakens this spatial constraint and promotes more non-local token influence.
papers.selection_reason: Compares variable-length image tokenizers for compact latent sequences, relevant to efficient generative modeling.
papers.title: Patch-Derived or Register Tokens? Comparing Variable-Length Image Tokenizers
papers.tldr: Patch-derived tokens reconstruct images better under extreme compression, while register tokens excel for generative tasks; representation alignment can close or reverse this gap.

papers.abstract: Running deep models for medical image analysis at the point of care is challenging with standard architectures: convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are often too heavy for edge devices, while Vision Transformers (ViTs) require massive training datasets to compensate for missing inductive biases. This study investigates how far the dual-token distillation used to train data-efficient ViTs can be pushed when applied across architectures, from a CNN-based teacher into a lightweight ViT student. LiteMed-ViT is introduced as a dual-token ViT featuring a convolutional stem and a class-balanced distillation objective; at 0.234M parameters, LiteMed-ViT carries 47.8x fewer parameters than its ResNet18 teacher at a memory footprint of just 0.89 MB. Evaluated against three compact CNN baselines on three MedMNIST subsets of varying modality and class balance, LiteMed-ViT attains higher accuracy than all three baselines on BloodMNIST (95.05%) and two on PathMNIST (89.15%). Under MedMNIST-C corruptions, it is at least as robust as every compact CNN across all subsets, outperforming them on BloodMNIST and PathMNIST without declining in relative standing as severity increases. Particular attention is devoted to identifying the exact conditions where performance plateaus. On DermaMNIST, LiteMed-ViT's balanced accuracy remains up to 1.9 points below the strongest compact CNNs and does not benefit from higher input resolutions up to 224 pixels, where ResNet18 gains 12.6 points. Stronger teachers do not yield a more accurate student, and overconfident ones lower its DermaMNIST balanced accuracy unless calibrated.
authors: Shuaibu Shehu (SR University), Elijah M. Flomo (SR University), Mohammad Safiya (GITAM University), Anurodh Kumar (SR University), Subodh Kumar (Dr. KNS Memorial Institute of Medical Sciences)
bullets: Uses a CNN teacher to distill knowledge into a lightweight ViT with a convolutional stem and class-balanced dual-token objective.
Has 0.234M parameters and a 0.89 MB memory footprint—47.8× fewer parameters than its ResNet18 teacher.
Outperforms compact CNN baselines on BloodMNIST and some PathMNIST evaluations, while matching or exceeding their corruption robustness.
Performance plateaus on DermaMNIST: balanced accuracy remains up to 1.9 points below the strongest CNNs and does not improve with higher resolution.
Stronger or overconfident teachers do not necessarily improve the student; calibration is important for DermaMNIST.
papers.selection_reason: Focuses on a lightweight medical vision transformer with reduced parameters and memory, fitting efficient AI.
papers.title: Promise and Limits of Cross-Architecture Knowledge Distillation for Lightweight Medical Vision Transformers (LiteMed-ViT)
papers.tldr: LiteMed-ViT shows that cross-architecture distillation can produce an extremely small, robust medical ViT, though its benefits depend strongly on the task and teacher calibration.

papers.abstract: Lung tumor segmentation plays a vital role in early detection and treatment planning of lung cancer. Although state-of-the-art deep learning models achieve high dice score coefficients (DSC), each forward pass requires computing large amounts of floating point operations, making them computationally expensive, requiring GPU acceleration, and having slow inference speed, limiting real-world clinical deployment. We propose a lightweight, energy-efficient model that leverages the ENet architecture for its real-time inference capability and low computational cost, enhanced with UNet-style skip connections between encoder and decoder stages for feature reuse and the lightweight Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) for improved feature representation. The model is trained on publicly available data from The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA) via the Medical Segmentation Decathlon Challenge (MSD) and evaluated on the Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI) dataset. Our model achieves a DSC of 0.90812 (threshold of 0.5) with its compact architecture of 430,052 parameters and 0.549 Giga Multiply-Accumulate operations (GMAC), making it up to 10 times faster, requires 79 times less GMAC than UNet, and has 22 times fewer parameters than SegNet. These characteristics make it well-suited for deployment in clinical settings where computational resources are limited and decrease the cost of utilizing such a system. Additionally, the explainable AI technique of Grad-CAM is used to provide visual interpretability of the model's predictions and to identify regions where segmentation performance requires improvement.
authors: Sharan Thummagunti, Aayushi Padia, Abhiram Koppuravuri, Prabhu Prasad B M, G N Girish
bullets: Targets the high computational cost and slow inference of deep learning models for lung tumor segmentation.
Combines ENet with UNet-style skip connections and lightweight CBAM attention for efficient feature reuse and representation.
Trained on TCIA/MSD data and evaluated on the LIDC-IDRI dataset.
Achieves a DSC of 0.90812 with 430,052 parameters and 0.549 GMAC.
Uses Grad-CAM to interpret predictions and identify regions needing segmentation improvement.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a lightweight, energy-efficient segmentation model with drastically reduced parameters and FLOPs, fitting efficient AI.
papers.title: Energy Efficient Lung Tumor Segmentation with a modified CBAM ENet Skip Model
papers.tldr: A compact ENet-based lung tumor segmentation model with CBAM and skip connections achieves strong segmentation accuracy while substantially reducing computational cost for resource-constrained clinical deployment.

papers.abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs), which process both visual inputs and text queries, incur high inference costs due to the large number of visual tokens, making visual token pruning a natural approach for improving efficiency. Recent work has leveraged query information to guide token selection, often through heuristics derived from attention patterns or token dynamics. However, these approaches do not explicitly exploit the underlying structure of query-vision interactions. We address this gap by observing that the query-vision interaction matrix, naturally induced by the query and key projections already present in transformer attention, is effectively low-rank, with a small number of dominant latent interaction modes capturing query-relevant semantics. Motivated by this observation, we propose Query-Vision Decomposition (QViD), a novel training-free query-aware visual token pruning method that exploits this structure. Extensive experiments on both image and video understanding benchmarks show that QViD consistently improves performance under matched token budgets, with the largest gains appearing under aggressive compression regimes.
authors: Harshithanjani Athi, Sravan Kumar Ankireddy, Jianzhong Charlie Zhang, Hyeji Kim
bullets: Visual token counts make large VLM inference computationally expensive.
Existing query-aware pruning methods often rely on attention heuristics without modeling query–vision interaction structure explicitly.
QViD decomposes the query–vision interaction matrix into dominant latent modes that capture query-relevant semantics.
Experiments on image and video understanding benchmarks show consistent gains at matched token budgets, especially with aggressive compression.
papers.selection_reason: Directly addresses visual token pruning for efficiency in VLMs.
papers.title: Vision Token Pruning via Query-Vision Interaction Decomposition
papers.tldr: QViD is a training-free method that prunes visual tokens by exploiting low-rank query–vision interactions, improving VLM efficiency and performance under fixed token budgets.

papers.abstract: Generalist segmenters such as Cellpose-SAM (CPSAM) outline cells accurately across stains but slowly; watershed detectors such as QuPath's are fast but less accurate. In time-critical use, such as interactive retrieval of cells from a user-drawn region, CPSAM at the reference settings takes 58-303 s per measured 8192 x 8192 region on an RTX 4500 Ada GPU, beyond a seconds-scale interactive target. We distil CPSAM into SWIFT-Cell (SWIFT), a 0.63M-parameter U-Net trained only on CPSAM masks of 1,202 H&E and IHC tiles. On three 8192 x 8192 development regions SWIFT takes 2.0-5.2 s on 4 CPU cores in int8, 2.5-5.1x faster than QuPath's detector on the same cores, and 0.36-0.49 s on a GPU. Against human annotations on eight H&E, IHC and ISH sets it keeps 95% of CPSAM's panoptic quality (PQ) on PanNuke (0.593 vs. 0.627) and is level on NuCLS (0.546 vs. 0.540). On Ki-67 IHC masks scored to the outline centre it is 0.205 PQ above QuPath's better mode, 0.079 below CPSAM and 0.027 below InstanSeg (CI includes 0; at the outer edge 0.008 below CPSAM); on 212 pathologist-outlined nuclei in Ki-67 fields of 12 untouched patients its recall is 0.925 (CPSAM 0.920, InstanSeg 0.901; paired difference CIs include 0); one method-blinded pathologist accepted its outlines in 96% of 100 fields (60 from two development tissue patients, 40 hematology; CPSAM 83%, QuPath 53%; tissue 100% for SWIFT and CPSAM); on ER/PR points from 12 patients its detection F1 is 0.882 (CPSAM 0.896, InstanSeg 0.857), and on 4-reader PD-L1 points 0.83 (CPSAM 0.85, readers 0.87). SWIFT is close to CPSAM in accuracy and faster than watershed detection.
authors: Devansh Lalwani, Swapnil Bhat, Muralikrishna H H, Anand Reddy, Maulik Shah
bullets: Addresses the slow runtime of generalist segmentation for time-critical cell retrieval.
Uses a 0.63M-parameter U-Net trained on CPSAM-generated masks from H&E and IHC tiles.
Processes 8192×8192 regions in 2.0–5.2 seconds on four CPU cores and 0.36–0.49 seconds on GPU.
Retains roughly 95% of CPSAM’s panoptic quality on PanNuke and matches it on NuCLS, with strong results across additional pathology tasks.
Pathologist acceptance was 96% of fields, compared with 83% for CPSAM and 53% for QuPath in the reported blinded evaluation.
papers.selection_reason: Distilled lightweight segmentation model with large speedups; relevant to efficient inference.
papers.title: SWIFT-Cell: Segmentation Without Iterative Flow Tracking
papers.tldr: SWIFT-Cell distils CPSAM into a lightweight U-Net that delivers near-CPSAM cell segmentation accuracy at interactive speeds.

papers.abstract: Large-scale AI training increasingly relies on massive video datasets with random temporal sampling patterns. However, existing video storage paradigms are optimized for sequential playback and employ sophisticated inter-frame reference structures to maximize compression efficiency. When applied to the random-sampling workloads of AI training, these paradigms face substantial decoding-efficiency bottlenecks. Workarounds such as independent JPEG frames and short groups of pictures (GOPs) reduce decoding work at the cost of larger storage and transfer volumes. In this paper, we identify two sources of decode amplification: sequential reconstruction of unrelated frames and reconstruction of the reference chains required by sampled targets. We address both sources by co-designing the decoding schedule and video reference structure. Dependency-aware sparse decoding reconstructs only requested frames and their required references, skipping unrelated reconstruction without transcoding the source videos. Optional offline Dependency-Decoupled Random Access (DDRA) encoding further reduces reference reconstruction by restricting each interior frame to two bounding intra-coded anchors. Together, sparse decoding and DDRA retain inter-frame prediction while bounding reconstruction to at most three frames per requested target, independent of the intra period. Experiments on a large-scale robotics corpus show that, at comparable reconstruction quality, our method achieves $1.45\times$ the loading throughput of LeRobot v3 with 58.7% less media payload.
authors: Zetian Song, Qize Yu, Yue Chen, Bohan Zhou, Bowen Ping, Yuqi Ye, Haocheng Tang, Haotian Zhang, Qizhe Wang, Shiyu Huang, Jiaqi Zhang, Siwei Ma, Wen Gao
bullets: AI training’s random temporal sampling makes conventional sequentially optimized video codecs decode inefficiently.
Dependency-aware sparse decoding reconstructs only requested frames and necessary references, without transcoding source videos.
Optional DDRA encoding limits each interior frame to two bounding intra-coded anchors, reducing reference-chain reconstruction.
Together, the methods bound reconstruction to at most three frames per requested target, regardless of intra period.
On a large-scale robotics corpus, the approach achieved 1.45× LeRobot v3 loading throughput with 58.7% less media payload at comparable reconstruction quality.
papers.selection_reason: Reduces decoding and storage overhead for random video access in AI training; efficiency contribution.
papers.title: Rethinking Video Storage for AI Training: Breaking Cross-Frame Dependencies for Efficient Random Access
papers.tldr: A video storage and decoding design for AI training enables efficient random frame access by avoiding unnecessary inter-frame reconstruction while preserving compression benefits.

papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform tasks specified through natural-language instructions, but their large weight footprint challenges deployment on memory-constrained onboard platforms. Ultra-low-bit quantization reduces this footprint, yet preserving task performance and controlling weight recovery costs remain challenging. We propose Action-Guided Quantization, which combines action sensitivity with a measured proxy for weight recovery cost to allocate matrix bitwidths under storage budgets. Per-channel calibration compensates for quantization error, while a uniform bitwidth within each matrix preserves regular layouts. Bit-dependent grouped lossless coding reduces resident weight storage, and block-wise recovery limits temporary buffers. On LIBERO, AGQ achieves 92.7% task success at W3, exceeding AWQ and GPTQ by 1.2 and 3.7 percentage points, respectively, and retains 70.5% success at W2.5. An asymmetric configuration, denoted W1.5$^{*}$, uses W4 vision weights and a parameter-weighted average of 1.5 bits for language weights. With lossless coding, it achieves $6.10\times$ complete-model compression relative to BF16 while retaining 25.5% task success. Code and experimental results are available at https://github.com/Qiuxu00/AGQ
authors: Xuhong Qiu, Zhuoyu Wu, Qiawei Zheng, Wenhui Ou, Wenqi Fang, Rapha\"{e}l C. -W. Phan
bullets: Targets the large memory footprint of vision-language-action models on onboard, memory-constrained robots.
Allocates matrix bitwidths under storage budgets using action sensitivity and a proxy for weight recovery cost.
Uses per-channel calibration, matrix-uniform bitwidths, lossless coding, and block-wise recovery to reduce storage and recovery overhead.
On LIBERO, achieves 92.7% success at W3 and 70.5% at W2.5; W3 exceeds AWQ and GPTQ by 1.2 and 3.7 percentage points.
A W1.5* configuration with lossless coding provides 6.10× compression relative to BF16 while retaining 25.5% task success.
papers.selection_reason: Ultra-low-bit quantization for VLA models; directly relevant to embodied VLA and memory-efficient deployment.
papers.title: AGQ: Action-Guided Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.tldr: AGQ enables memory-efficient VLA deployment by allocating ultra-low-bit weights according to action sensitivity and recovery cost while preserving task performance.

papers.abstract: We introduce Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, a hybrid Mamba-Transformer vision-language model that optimizes speed and intelligence per GB of memory used for local agentic workloads. Derived from the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B model family, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB combines Star Elastic compression with 2-bit Quantization-Aware Distillation for memory-constrained deployment. The model is optimized for reasoning, agentic tool use, and web & terminal interactions. We also trained a LiLiCorr speculative drafter that is released alongside the model to reach our target inference speed. The resulting model achieves a higher accuracy than leading models with similar memory footprints and speed across many benchmarks for general agentic capabilities (e.g., GDPVal v2), web browsing (e.g., BrowseComp), and terminal use (e.g., Terminal-Bench 2.1), with a relatively high TPS of 84 on RTX Spark that is comparable to models with much lower active parameter counts and more than sufficient for long-horizon agentic applications.
authors: Ganesh Ajjanagadde, Chris Alexiuk, Luke Alonso, Kumar Anshuman, Maor Ashkenazi, Nave Assaf, Gorkem Batmaz, Omer Belhasin, Shai Ben Nun, Akhiad Bercovich, Pritam Biswas, Caroline Blanco, Tijmen Blankevoort, Michael Boone, Christopher Borden, Kari Briski, Bryan Catanzaro, Zijia Chen, Aishwarya Chhabra, Hung-Yueh Chiang, Annamalai Chockalingam, Jonathan Cohen, Joey Conway, Olivier Delalleau, Gerardo Delgado Cabrera, Leon Derczynski, Li Ding, Will Efstratis, Michael Elad, Ellie Evans, Wes Feely, Michael Fukuyama, Gaurav Garg, Rishabh Garg, Arvind Gopalakrishnan, Shishir Goyal, Kartik Gulia, Hao Guo, Negar Habibi, Scott Hara, Ehsan Hosseini Asl, Rohit Jena, Udi Karpas, Bilal Kartal, Mayank Kaushik, Manoj Kilaru, Mackenzie Kosseim, Oleksii Kuchaiev, Matthieu Le, Raymond Lee, Jian Leong, Jonathan Li, Sheldon Liang, Mingjie Liu, Eileen Long, Katherine Luna, Chenjie Luo, Mingyuan Ma, Arsh Maknojia, Richard Mazzarese, Jessica Medina, Puhui Meng, Yoav Miron, Pavlo Molchanov, David Mosallanezhad, Chetan Mungekar, Marina Neseem, Oluwatobi Olabiyi, Jason Paul, Bhavesh Pawar, Seth Poulos, Anav Prasad, Meredith Price, Sweta Priyadarshi, Haifeng Qian, Vinay Raman, Kaustubh Rao, Hayley Ross, Matan Rusanovsky, Sudeep Sabnis, Karan Sapra, Micah Schaffer, Schmitty, Alex Settle, Ashton Sharabiani, Haran Kumar Shiv Kumar, Rameshwar Shivbhakta, Guillermo Siman, Barnaby Simkin, Oliver Simons, Andrii Skliar, Padmavathy Subramanian, Yoshi Suhara, Ali Taghibakhshi, Nima Tajbakhsh, Andrew Tao, Roy Uziel, Prasoon Varshney, Jose Vergara, Huy Vu, Mengru Wang, Rochelle Woods, Pinky Xu, Dina Yared, Chenhan Yu, Chaosen Zhang, Jian Zhang, Yiheng Zhang, Ran Zilberstein
bullets: Targets reasoning, tool use, web browsing, and terminal interactions for local deployment.
Combines a hybrid Mamba-Transformer architecture with Star Elastic compression and 2-bit Quantization-Aware Distillation.
Includes a LiLiCorr speculative drafter to improve inference speed.
Reports strong accuracy across agentic, web-browsing, and terminal-use benchmarks, with 84 TPS on RTX Spark.
Scope: optimized for memory-constrained local workloads rather than general-purpose deployment claims beyond the reported benchmarks.
papers.selection_reason: Hybrid vision-language model optimized for local memory-constrained deployment with compression and speculative decoding.
papers.title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB: A Hybrid Vision-Language Model for Local AI
papers.tldr: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is a compressed hybrid vision-language model designed for fast, capable local agentic AI under tight memory limits.

papers.abstract: Multilingual tokenizers trained on English-dominated corpora often over-segment Indic languages, resulting in longer token sequences and increased tokenization disparity across scripts. We present AdaptTok-Indic, an Indic-specialized extension of adaptive tokenization that combines Unicode-normalized preprocessing with explicit Indic conjunct handling, script-aware routing, and learned byte-level boundary prediction jointly trained with a small Transformer language model. Evaluated on Bengali and Hindi, with additional evaluation on Gujarati, Tamil, and Telugu, AdaptTok-Indic achieves lower token fertility than SentencePiece BPE, an Indic-oriented tokenizer baseline, and an independently implemented MAGNET-style baseline. Across five recorded seeds, mean fertility is 1.432 for Bengali and 1.388 for Hindi, compared with 2.156 and 2.085 for SentencePiece BPE. Recorded downstream scores average 57.69 on evaluated Indic settings versus 50.82 for the SentencePiece BPE configuration. Independent verification runs using the released prototype confirm the same directional trends. The current implementation is a small-scale prototype with documented simplifications, and no statistical significance testing, released-MAGNET comparison, or code-mixed evaluation is performed. These results suggest that Indic-specialized adaptive segmentation can reduce tokenization disparity while maintaining competitive downstream performance.
authors: Binayak Mukherjeea, Moitreya Nandi, Arindam Panja
bullets: Targets over-segmentation of Indic languages by English-dominated multilingual tokenizers.
Combines Unicode normalization, Indic conjunct handling, script-aware routing, and learned byte-level boundary prediction.
Evaluated on Bengali, Hindi, Gujarati, Tamil, and Telugu; reported fertility is lower than the compared baselines.
Downstream scores also favor the proposed configuration on the evaluated Indic settings, with independent runs confirming the directional trends.
Scope is limited to a small-scale prototype without significance testing, a released-MAGNET comparison, or code-mixed evaluation.
papers.selection_reason: Indic-specialized adaptive tokenization reduces token fertility and sequence length, relevant to efficient language modeling.
papers.title: AdaptTok-Indic: Script-Aware Adaptive Tokenization for Indic Languages
papers.tldr: AdaptTok-Indic reduces token over-segmentation and tokenization disparity for Indic languages through script-aware adaptive tokenization, with prototype evaluations showing favorable fertility and downstream trends.

papers.abstract: We present HyScale, a long-context training system for learned sparse attention. Learned sparse attention is a promising architecture for million-token contexts, widely adopted in production since DeepSeek-V3.2. Selection, however, grows into the training bottleneck. For each query, it scores every previous token whereas sparse attention reads only $k$; worse, current systems materialize a full score table and repeat selection during recomputation. Our key insight is that the output of selection is not an activation, but rather a set of indices. Building on it, HyScale introduces HyTopK and selection replay. HyTopK finds each query's exact top-$k$ on the fly without a score table, while selection replay reuses forward-pass selection in recomputation. Together with holistic system optimizations tackling end-to-end training challenges, HyScale speeds up GLM-5.1 training on 1M-token sequences by 2.07$\times$ over Megatron-LM on 512 H20 GPUs. It also speeds up the CSA layers of DeepSeek-V4-Flash and the QSA layers of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next by 2.01$\times$ and 1.57$\times$ at 1M tokens on 32 H800 GPUs.
authors: Yangshen Deng, Xinjing Huang, Yulong Wang, Yunzhuo Liu, Jun Hu, Shuyong Tan, Chun-Chih Tseng, Mingji Han, Ray Ying, Key Zhang, Luo Mai
bullets: Learned sparse attention makes selection a training bottleneck because each query scores all prior tokens, despite reading only top-k tokens.
HyTopK computes exact top-k indices on the fly without materializing a full score table.
Selection replay reuses forward-pass selection during recomputation, reducing redundant work.
Combined with end-to-end system optimizations, HyScale achieves reported speedups of 2.07×, 2.01×, and 1.57× on 1M-token training workloads.
The evaluation covers GLM-5.1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash CSA layers, and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA layers on H20 and H800 GPUs.
papers.selection_reason: System for scaling learned sparse attention training directly targets efficient attention and long-context models.
papers.title: HyScale: Scaling Long-Context Training for Learned Sparse Attention
papers.tldr: HyScale accelerates million-token training for learned sparse attention by avoiding full score tables and replaying selection during recomputation.

papers.abstract: Agentic VLM pipelines increasingly pass the same static visual evidence through multiple specialist agents and tools. This design creates an orchestration-level redundancy mode: semantically unchanged images are repeatedly reconstructed as image-conditioned requests at the VLM API boundary. We call this phenomenon visual orchestration tax and develop a measurement-to-certification framework for visual evidence reuse in agentic VLM pipelines. The audit side defines $\mathrm{M1}_{\mathrm{trace}}$ to count raw visual-evidence touches and M2 to measure structural touch redundancy, with query-level distributions, bootstrap confidence intervals, and paired quality tests. Across SeeingEye and MAMMQA on chart, document, general-VQA, and multi-modal-QA tasks, audits reveal 66.8-75.6% visual-evidence touch redundancy, and every audited query exceeds the predefined gate. The certification side introduces SharedVisCache, a contract-aware evidence reuse hook keyed by image content, preprocessing fingerprint, and encoder assumptions. On SeeingEye, contract validation certifies 75.0-75.5% repeated touches as reusable while preserving 350/350 output strings and $Δ\mathrm{M5}{=}0$. At the physical layer, certified hits reduce $F_{\mathrm{vision}}$ from 800 to 200 in ChartQA-200 trace replay and from 200 to 50 inside live SeeingEye translator-stage physical integration, preserving 800/800 replay strings and 200/200 integrated call outputs. The results position visual reuse as a measurable, behavior-preserving property of agent orchestration and define an agent-layer contract that makes backend prefix or token reuse semantically interpretable.
bullets: Introduces the “visual orchestration tax”: semantically unchanged images are repeatedly reconstructed at VLM API boundaries.
Defines audit metrics M1_trace and M2 for counting visual-evidence touches and structural redundancy, with distributional and paired-quality analyses.
Audits across SeeingEye and MAMMQA find 66.8–75.6% visual-evidence touch redundancy, with every query exceeding the predefined gate.
Proposes SharedVisCache, a contract-aware cache keyed by image content, preprocessing, and encoder assumptions.
Certification preserves tested outputs while reducing physical vision computations from 800 to 200 in replay and from 200 to 50 in live integration.
papers.selection_reason: Audits and caches redundant visual evidence in agentic VLM pipelines, reducing vision compute.
papers.title: Visual Orchestration Tax in Agentic VLM Pipelines: Auditing and Certifying Visual Evidence Reuse
papers.tldr: The paper measures redundant reuse of unchanged visual evidence in agentic VLM pipelines and certifies safe caching that substantially reduces vision processing while preserving outputs.

papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to optimize code for performance. This practice often assumes that improvements in execution speed naturally translate into overall lower energy consumption. We challenge this assumption empirically by measuring whether performance-optimized code produced by LLM self-refinement pipelines is also energy-efficient relative to canonical human reference solutions, and whether the energy cost of the optimization process can be offset by subsequent execution-time savings. We evaluate 11 open-source models across four decoding configurations on all 1,000 problems of EffiBench, a state-of-the-art performance benchmark, while collecting per-process, hardware-level energy measurements throughout. Inference energy spans 0.79 to 8.68 MJ across model-variant pairs, which is roughly equivalent to the energy of 250 to 2800 GPT-4.1 queries. Limiting the maximum number of output tokens has the largest impact, reducing energy use by up to 69% compared to the default configuration. On the execution side, 42 of 44 configurations produce code that consumes more energy per problem than the canonical human reference, with overheads ranging from +4% to +886%. The two exceptions achieve only marginal gains, with break-even points on the order of 10^6 to 10^7 executions. Mixture-of-Experts architectures consume substantially less inference energy than equivalently-sized dense models without sacrificing correctness, making architectural choice a more consequential sustainability lever than decoding parameters. Performance optimization and energy efficiency are not always aligned goals: LLM self-refinement consistently produces faster-seeking but energy-heavier code relative to what a human engineer would write. All artifacts are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23598170.
authors: Sadra Emami, Benjamin Weigell, Mohammad Reza Mousavi, Gunel Jahangirova, Hugo Araujo, Bernhard Bauer
bullets: The study evaluates 11 open-source models across four decoding configurations on 1,000 EffiBench problems with hardware-level energy monitoring.
Optimization inference consumes 0.79–8.68 MJ per model-configuration pair; limiting output length reduces this energy by up to 69%.
42 of 44 configurations generate code that uses more energy per execution than canonical human solutions, with overheads from 4% to 886%.
The two energy-saving configurations require roughly 10^6–10^7 executions to offset optimization energy costs.
Mixture-of-Experts models use less inference energy than similarly sized dense models without sacrificing correctness.
papers.selection_reason: Empirical study of LLM inference and generated-code energy use; directly informs energy-efficient AI deployment and decoding choices.
papers.title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations
papers.tldr: LLM-driven code optimization often reduces runtime at the cost of substantially higher energy use, including during both inference and execution.

papers.abstract: Low-rank SVD-based compression offers a powerful strategy to reduce the computational costs of LLMs. However, existing methods face two key limitations: (i) global rank allocation, where uncalibrated error proxies fail to capture complex error propagation, and (ii) decomposition quality, where Fisher-based estimators suffer from severe rank collapse. In this work, we address these limitations by introducing Layer-wise Error Modeling Search (LEMS) and KFAC-SVD. LEMS advances rank allocation by introducing a layer-wise error surrogate that integrates local and global layer importance alongside a propagation bias, enabling effective global rank allocation via an ILP formulation. KFAC-SVD improves decomposition quality by utilizing token-wise statistics, mitigating the rank deficiency observed in prior Fisher-based SVD approaches. Across Mistral, Qwen3, and Llama 3 model families, we show that LEMS consistently outperforms existing search strategies, delivering significant zero-shot accuracy gains of up to 4.8 p.p. that generalize to model sizes of 70B parameters, while KFAC-SVD achieves an average perplexity improvement of 15%. Project page and code: https://lems-svd.github.io
authors: Moritz Thoma, Maximilian Groezinger, Maximilian Forstenh\"ausler, Emad Aghajanzadeh, Manoj Rohit Vemparala, Christos Anagnostopoulos, Pierpaolo Mori, Nael Fasfous, Alexander Frickenstein, Daniel Mueller-Gritschneder, Ulf Schlichtmann
bullets: Addresses inaccurate global rank allocation and rank collapse in Fisher-based SVD compression.
LEMS models layer-wise local/global importance and error propagation, then allocates ranks using an ILP.
KFAC-SVD uses token-wise statistics to mitigate rank deficiency during decomposition.
Evaluated on Mistral, Qwen3, and Llama 3 families, with gains extending to models up to 70B parameters.
Reports up to 4.8 percentage-point zero-shot accuracy gains from LEMS and a 15% average perplexity improvement from KFAC-SVD.
papers.selection_reason: Advances SVD-based LLM compression through layer-wise error modeling search, offering a method to reduce computational costs and memory usage in large models.
papers.title: Advancing SVD-based LLM Compression via Layer-Wise Error Model Search
papers.tldr: LEMS and KFAC-SVD improve SVD-based LLM compression by allocating ranks more effectively and producing higher-quality low-rank decompositions.

papers.abstract: Fine-tuning on datasets of unknown origin can create a backdoor in the trained model when the data includes poisoned examples. Difficult to localise and remove, backdoors can persist through safety training. While parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods capture the full parameter changes introduced during training, they are not easily interpretable. We present the full method of TopKLoRA, extending the preliminary proposal of Masiak et al. (2025), an interpretable-by-design LoRA variant in which only the $k$ largest adapter latents are active at each token. Unlike SAEs, TopKLoRA is trained purely on downstream loss, where optimisation pressure incentivises learning functionally causal latents. We demonstrate this sparse LoRA adapter in a sleeper-agent backdoor case study where we create model organisms by fine-tuning gemma-2-2b, Qwen2.5-1.5B, and Qwen2.5-7B on a poisoned instruction-following dataset. For each organism, we identify and ablate a circuit that is both necessary and sufficient to implement the backdoor. Furthermore, our new fine-tuning method produces sparse circuits that are up to an order of magnitude smaller than a dense LoRA baseline, allowing surgical ablation of the malicious capability without sacrificing instruction-following performance. Finally, we propose a technique to construct model organisms with localised circuits using TopKLoRA latents and gradient-routing, which we use to validate the findings of our circuit search algorithm. We consider these findings as a step toward interpretable-by-design architectures that provide faithful units of analysis without compromising model performance. We share our code: https://github.com/interpretable-finetuning/TopKLoRA.
authors: Marek Masiak, Andrzej Szablewski, Nicola Cancedda, Constantin Venhoff
bullets: Targets backdoors introduced by poisoned fine-tuning data, which can be difficult to localise and remove.
Activates only the k largest adapter latents per token and trains solely with downstream loss.
Produces sparse, functionally causal circuits that are up to an order of magnitude smaller than dense LoRA circuits.
In sleeper-agent model organisms based on Gemma and Qwen models, identified circuits were necessary and sufficient for the backdoor.
Ablating these circuits removed the malicious capability without sacrificing instruction-following performance; scope is demonstrated through backdoor case studies.
papers.selection_reason: Sparse interpretable LoRA with k-active latents offers a transferable efficiency and interpretability technique for LLM fine-tuning and circuit analysis.
papers.title: Interpretable sparse fine-tuning with TopKLoRA enables faithful circuit discovery
papers.tldr: TopKLoRA makes LoRA fine-tuning sparse and interpretable, enabling faithful identification and surgical removal of backdoor circuits while preserving normal instruction following.

papers.abstract: Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) offer strong zero-shot forecasting capabilities, but their high pretraining cost raises a practical sustainability question: does this upfront investment pay off over a full deployment lifecycle, compared to supervised standalone models that must be periodically retrained? We model the cumulative carbon cost of different approaches across a realistic industrial scenario: Chronos-2 amortizes its pretraining cost within months for large or frequently queried deployments, but a classical model remains cheaper indefinitely for small or rarely queried ones. For cases where reducing the TSFM's own cost matters, we show that removing a single encoder block (7.9% of parameters) via a gradient-free pruning criterion yields a consistent 6 to 9% reduction in FLOPs, CO2 emissions, and latency, at essentially no cost to zero-shot forecasting performance across a 25-task benchmark.
authors: C\'ecile Luc, Nathana\"el Lemonnier, Ievgen Redko
bullets: Frames TSFM sustainability as a lifecycle comparison between upfront pretraining and recurring retraining.
Chronos-2 amortizes its pretraining carbon cost within months for large or frequently queried deployments.
Classical standalone models remain cheaper indefinitely for small or rarely queried deployments.
Removing one encoder block (7.9% of parameters) cuts FLOPs, emissions, and latency by 6–9%.
Pruning preserves essentially unchanged zero-shot forecasting performance across 25 tasks.
papers.selection_reason: Addresses sustainability and efficiency in Time Series Foundation Models by proposing a gradient-free pruning criterion to reduce FLOPs, CO2 emissions, and latency.
papers.title: Sustainability of TSFM Deployment and Pretraining: From Carbon Footprint Analysis to Mitigation via Pruning
papers.tldr: TSFM pretraining can become more carbon-efficient than repeated supervised retraining at scale, while pruning reduces deployment costs with negligible forecasting impact.

papers.abstract: Agent harnesses repeatedly invoke reasoning after tool feedback, even when an earlier call has already fixed the next action. We introduce HarnessMM (Harness Minus Minus), a method for improving harness token efficiency through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement (RSI). RSI iteratively refines companion harness configurations from training feedback, with validation selecting the configuration for deployment. A controller at the model-tool boundary reuses resolved decisions to replace later reasoning callbacks while actor weights remain fixed. Executable Decision Graphs store exact actions, literal arguments, causal dependencies, and public guards. Guarded Decision Reuse activates these persistent decisions from observed receipts; Certified Callback Substitution executes them through the native interface and records removal of the registered slow callback. New semantic decisions, unsupported evidence, and selector abstention invoke the original actor again. The representation restricts what feedback may change, while complete-task measurements establish quality and cost. On HumanEval, HarnessMM preserves Codex success at 90.82\% while reducing Tokens/task (k) from 66.72 to 47.02 (29.54\% saving). For DeepSeek Harness, success rises from 71.43\% to 85.71\% while Tokens/task (k) fall from 96.28 to 11.62 (87.93\% saving). A separate MBPP ablation measures 26.91\% lower cost than single-use graphs and 19.52\% lower cost than retained callbacks. These results establish guarded decision reuse as a practical way to reduce repeated reasoning in existing harnesses.
authors: Yuhua Jiang, Chang Xu, Feifei Gao, Li Zhao
bullets: Targets harnesses that unnecessarily re-invoke reasoning after tool feedback has already determined the next action.
Uses recursive self-improvement to refine harness configurations, with validation selecting the deployment configuration while keeping actor weights fixed.
Stores exact actions and dependencies in Executable Decision Graphs; guarded reuse and certified callback substitution replace eligible reasoning callbacks.
On HumanEval, preserves 90.82% success while reducing tokens per task by 29.54%; on DeepSeek Harness, raises success to 85.71% and cuts tokens by 87.93%.
MBPP ablations report lower cost than single-use graphs and retained callbacks, though reuse is bypassed for novel decisions, unsupported evidence, or selector abstention.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a method for improving token efficiency in LLM agent harnesses through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement, directly addressing token management and efficiency.
papers.title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
papers.tldr: HarnessMM reduces repeated agent reasoning by safely reusing previously resolved tool decisions while preserving or improving task success.

papers.abstract: Split inference partitions a Vision Transformer between a resource-constrained edge device and a server. However, transmitting intermediate tokens across the communication channel is costly. Deploying fine-tuned backbones to every endpoint becomes expensive as well. We study token reduction for split inference under a frozen backbone, where only a small adapter is shipped. We observe that the CLS token plays a dual role: it acts as the global summary the receiver needs for classification, and it serves as a signal on which patches to keep. We propose Consomm\'e, a method utilizing both characteristics. There, an information bottleneck compresses the CLS token into a compact latent which is transmitted in place of the full CLS token and conditions a learned patch gate merging patches into exactly $k$ tokens via soft assignment. It reaches any budget in a single step, thus escaping the per-layer cap of bipartite matching (BPM). On DeiT-S/T, it leads all methods at aggressive token budgets and remains operable at shallow splits where BPM cannot operate, while matching fine-tuned methods at gentle budgets at a fraction of their deployment cost.
bullets: Targets split inference with a frozen backbone, avoiding deployment of separately fine-tuned backbones.
Uses an information bottleneck to transmit a compact CLS representation instead of the full CLS token.
Conditions a learned patch gate on this representation to softly merge patches into any desired token budget in one step.
On DeiT-S/T, performs best at aggressive budgets, works at shallow splits where BPM cannot, and matches fine-tuned methods at gentler budgets with lower deployment cost.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes conditioned token merging for split inference, a clear token-level efficiency contribution.
papers.title: Consomm\'e: Conditioned Token Merging for Split Inference
papers.tldr: Consommé reduces communication in split-inference Vision Transformers by compressing the CLS token and conditionally merging patches into exactly k tokens using only a small adapter.

papers.abstract: The rapid growth of video data has created an urgent need for efficient video understanding systems that can handle long and continuous visual inputs, posing significant challenges for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) due to severe memory bottlenecks. Moreover, existing compression methods often overlook the explosive accumulation of approximation errors. To address this issue, we propose Video-MemComp, a training-free and sensitivity-aware context management framework for memory-constrained streaming video understanding. Our method theoretically decomposes compression error into orthogonal local approximation error and layer-wise structural sensitivity via a first-order Taylor expansion. To minimize local approximation error, we perform token aggregation in a pre-RoPE safe zone with an attention-conserving logit bias, mitigating geometric distortions caused by RoPE rotations. To manage layer-wise structural sensitivity, we dynamically allocate the KV cache budget based on offline gradient priors and online context entropy, prioritizing high-sensitivity layers. Video-MemComp outperforms or achieves performance comparable to full-cache and state-of-the-art compression methods on benchmarks including MLVU, VideoMME, and EgoSchema. Notably, it improves the overall accuracy of Qwen2.5-VL-3B from 62.3% to 64.1% while reducing the KV cache to an equivalent of 6,000 tokens per layer, saving over 90% of KV memory.
authors: Yonghui Niu, Yuhao Ji, Chang Nie, Jiao Zhang, Yilong Li, Junlan Feng, Ran He, Caifeng Shan, Chaoyou Fu
bullets: Targets memory bottlenecks and error accumulation in long-context streaming video understanding.
Uses a first-order Taylor expansion to separate local approximation error from layer-wise structural sensitivity.
Aggregates tokens in a pre-RoPE safe zone with attention-conserving logit bias to reduce geometric distortion.
Dynamically allocates KV-cache budgets using offline gradient priors and online context entropy.
Matches or exceeds full-cache and existing compression methods on MLVU, VideoMME, and EgoSchema; Qwen2.5-VL-3B rises from 62.3% to 64.1% with over 90% KV-memory savings.
papers.selection_reason: Directly addresses streaming-video KV-cache and token compression for efficient MLLM inference.
papers.title: Video-MemComp: Taylor-Guided Sensitivity-Aware Memory Management for Streaming Video Understanding
papers.tldr: Video-MemComp is a training-free method that compresses streaming-video KV memory by modeling sensitivity and approximation error, achieving over 90% memory savings with improved accuracy on Qwen2.5-VL-3B.

papers.abstract: Quality-Aware Decoding (QAD) improves machine translation through test-time scaling, generating multiple candidate translations and selecting the final output with a quality-aware decoder. Usually the same candidate budget N is spent on every source sentence, assuming that all inputs require the same amount of search. We show that this assumption does not hold and that the quality gain obtained from additional candidates varies across sentences. We study search utility through three quantities: total scaling gain, how much quality a sentence can gain from a much larger candidate pool; marginal scaling gain, the expected gain from generating one additional batch of candidates; and the sampling saturation point, the candidate budget required to realize most of the total scaling gain. We investigate two sources of information for predicting these quantities: signals available before candidate-set expansion, and statistics computed from the candidate pool accumulated during search. We find that sentence-level signals correlate with total scaling gain but are less informative about the sampling saturation point. In contrast, properties of the current candidate pool provide useful signals of marginal scaling gain. Finally, we show that these signals can identify sentences that obtain larger gains when additional search is selectively applied.
authors: Javier Garcia Gilabert, Rico Sennrich, Andr\'e F. T. Martins
bullets: Quality-aware decoding does not benefit equally from the same candidate budget on every input.
The study defines total scaling gain, marginal scaling gain, and the sampling saturation point to characterize search utility.
Pre-expansion sentence-level signals predict potential total gain but are weaker for predicting when search will saturate.
Statistics from candidates accumulated during search provide useful estimates of marginal gain.
These signals support selectively applying additional search to sentences likely to benefit most.
papers.selection_reason: Adaptive allocation of test-time search budget for MT offers transferable efficiency insights for inference-time compute reduction.
papers.title: When is more search useful? An Empirical Study of Search Utility in Quality-Aware Decoding for Machine Translation
papers.tldr: Search benefits vary by sentence, and candidate-pool signals can help allocate extra translation search where it is most useful.

papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) read images through visual tokens, and under the small per-image budgets that efficient deployment requires, the fine text of documents, charts and infographics becomes illegible. Zooming in recovers the evidence, but the region must be chosen before the model answers. We find that MLLMs know where the evidence is, but not in a form that can be read before they answer: the answer tokens localize it from the middle layers on, whereas the attention available before answering does so only in the top layers, at a depth that varies across models, and diffusely. Supervising the pre-answer attention to point degrades reading, and the benefit of zooming is governed by each image's information gap. Building on these findings, we introduce ours, which lets an MLLM look where its answer would. A dedicated look token, processed in a single prefill and kept out of the answering pass, learns in hindsight to attend as the model's own correct answers do, extracting this knowledge into a concentrated pointer before any answer exists. Its hidden state then selects how to look, from no zoom to crops, square windows, windows that adapt to the pointer and foveated warps, supervised by the counterfactual outcome of every view. ours needs no box annotations, per-model layer search, external localizers or generation before the answer. On Qwen3-VL at three scales and five text-rich benchmarks, it surpasses the strongest baseline by 4.8-9.1 points at 98 visual tokens per view and attention-guided zooming by 11.1-17.0 points, while running faster than attention-guided and grounding-based zooming.
authors: Zhensheng Hu, Guanglong Xu, Guanqiang Hu
bullets: Small visual-token budgets make fine text in documents, charts, and infographics difficult to read.
Answer tokens localize relevant evidence earlier and more clearly than pre-answer attention, whose useful depth varies by model.
OURS uses a dedicated look token trained from correct-answer attention to produce a concentrated pointer before answering.
The pointer selects among no zoom, crops, adaptive windows, square windows, and foveated warps using counterfactual view outcomes.

On Qwen3-VL across three scales and five text-rich benchmarks, it improves over the strongest baseline by 4.8–9.1 points and attention-guided zooming by 11.1–17.0 points at 98 visual tokens per view, while running faster than both attention-guided and grounding-based zooming.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a mechanism for MLLMs to intelligently zoom into images before answering, optimizing visual token usage. This addresses spatial intelligence (understanding where to look) and efficient AI (token budget management).
papers.title: The Answer Knows Where to Look: Zooming before MLLMs Answer under Visual-Token Budgets
papers.tldr: OURS lets MLLMs identify where answer-critical visual evidence lies before answering, enabling effective zooming under tight visual-token budgets.

papers.abstract: LLM inference is increasingly deployed as a core service for enterprise and interactive applications, but sovereignty, compliance, latency and resource-locality requirements can limit the suitability of centralised cloud deployments. Telco operators offer geographically distributed compute and network infrastructure for addressing these constraints. However, existing LLM serving frameworks are designed for tightly coupled data centres and provide limited support for coordinating geographically distributed and heterogeneous resources. We present InferSlice, a reference architecture for Service-Level Objective (SLO)-driven LLM inference over a telco infrastructure, integrating network slicing, GPU partitioning, elastic serving and observability. Led by BT in collaboration with the University of Bristol and NVIDIA, and realised on the JOINER UK national-scale wide-area network (WAN), InferSlice is evaluated on service differentiation across tiers, elastic scale-out, client-edge bandwidth as a bottleneck, and the reach of tensor, pipeline, data parallelism, and prefill/decode disaggregation over the WAN. Our results show that, on a general-purpose telco network, tiers yield distinct latency-throughput regimes, and weight streaming shortens scale-out time. Replication is placement-insensitive but memory-bound; pipeline parallelism tolerates near- and mid-cross-site hops, while tensor parallelism and disaggregation fail beyond a single subnet hop. We share practical insights from operating SLO-driven inference on a telco network, lessons learned and open questions, and hope to encourage further research on distributed and heterogeneous LLM inference systems.
authors: Juan Parra-Ullauri, Anthony Chiu, Hari Madhukumar, Zhaozhou Wu, Anderson Bravalheri, Alex Healing, Andy Corston-Petrie, Dimitra Simeonidou, Nektaria Efthymiou
bullets: Addresses sovereignty, compliance, latency, and resource-locality constraints that limit centralized cloud inference.
Combines network slicing, GPU partitioning, elastic serving, and observability for SLO-driven operation.
Evaluated on the JOINER UK wide-area network across service tiers, elastic scale-out, bandwidth bottlenecks, and distributed parallelism strategies.

Findings: service tiers create distinct latency-throughput regimes; weight streaming speeds scale-out; replication is memory-bound; pipeline parallelism tolerates near- and mid-site hops, while tensor parallelism and prefill/decode disaggregation require a single subnet hop.
Provides operational insights, lessons learned, and open questions for distributed LLM inference over telco networks.
papers.selection_reason: SLO-driven distributed LLM inference over wide-area networks reduces latency and improves resource efficiency, fitting the efficient-AI scope.
papers.title: InferSlice: A Reference Architecture for SLO-driven LLM Inference over a Telco Wide-Area Network
papers.tldr: InferSlice is a reference architecture for meeting LLM inference SLOs across geographically distributed, heterogeneous telco infrastructure.

papers.abstract: Instruction-based image editing models exhibit pronounced sample-specific performance variation: different models can produce substantially different results for the same source image and editing instruction, and the best-performing model often varies across requests. These models also differ substantially in inference latency, making fixed-model deployment inefficient. We therefore study image editing model routing, which dynamically selects an editor from a candidate pool given an input image and editing instruction. We introduce EditJev, a System One routing model that directly predicts sample-level preference scores over candidate image editing models in a single forward pass. A lightweight preference head on a vision-language backbone produces a fixed-dimensional score vector without autoregressive model-name generation or response parsing. To train EditJev, we construct pairwise preferences from offline candidate outputs and optimize a pairwise ranking objective to learn relative model suitability. At inference time, EditJev combines the predicted preference scores with model-level speed scores to balance editing quality and generation latency. Experiments on ImgEdit and GEdit-En show that EditJev improves aggregate quality over the strongest fixed editor, from 4.540 to 4.592 and from 8.194 to 8.255, respectively, while reducing estimated end-to-end latency by 60.8% and 31.7%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of direct, structured model routing for efficient image editing.
authors: Zhile Guan, Xu Jiang, Yule Duan, Gongbo Zhang, Shuyu Wang, Xiao Chen, Jian Zhang
bullets: Image editing models vary significantly in performance across individual images and instructions, and also differ in inference speed.
EditJev predicts preference scores for all candidate editors in one forward pass using a vision-language backbone with a lightweight preference head.
It learns relative model suitability from pairwise preferences derived from offline candidate outputs.
Routing combines predicted quality preferences with model speed scores to balance editing quality and latency.
On ImgEdit and GEdit-En, EditJev improves aggregate quality while reducing estimated end-to-end latency by 60.8% and 31.7%, respectively.
papers.selection_reason: Sample-level routing among image editing models directly reduces inference latency while preserving quality, constituting a transferable efficient-inference contribution.
papers.title: EditJev: System One Routing for Image Editing Models
papers.tldr: EditJev routes each image-editing request to a suitable model, improving quality over the best fixed editor while substantially reducing latency.

papers.abstract: Geospatial foundation models (GeoFMs) are costly to pretrain, yet model families often repeat this process across backbone scales and sensing modalities. We investigate feature distillation as a more efficient way to reuse existing representations. First, we distill frozen CROMA and TerraMind teachers into smaller Vision Transformers through patch-level feature matching. Across nine PANGAEA tasks, distilled TerraMind Tiny, Small, and Base outperform their scale-matched released counterparts by 2.76, 3.02, and 1.87 mean IoU points, respectively; each also matches or exceeds the next-larger released model. Distilled CROMA-Base gains 2.05 points. TerraMind-Base required only 43 A6000 GPU-hours, approximately 0.5\% of the reported cost of independent pretraining. Second, we introduce TEDI, an unpaired multi-expert approach combining TerraMind for multispectral imagery and DINOv3 for high-resolution RGB. Separate patch embeddings route unpaired inputs into a shared Transformer trunk, removing the need for co-registered data. TEDI-Large achieves the highest single-model mean in our PANGAEA-9 comparison (62.51 mIoU), outperforming both teachers overall while retaining their modality-specific strengths. TEDI-Base reaches 61.75 mIoU with 72\% fewer parameters. These results show that distillation improves the GeoFM accuracy-compute frontier while consolidating complementary experts into a single versatile backbone.
authors: Mario Hamon, Pierre Adorni, Minh-Tan Pham
bullets: Distills frozen CROMA and TerraMind teachers into smaller Vision Transformers using patch-level feature matching.
Across nine PANGAEA tasks, distilled TerraMind and CROMA models improve over scale-matched released models and often reach the performance of larger ones.
TerraMind-Base distillation used approximately 0.5% of the reported cost of training an independent model.
TEDI combines TerraMind’s multispectral expertise with DINOv3’s high-resolution RGB features through separate patch embeddings and a shared Transformer trunk, without co-registered data.
TEDI-Large achieves the highest reported PANGAEA-9 single-model mean, while TEDI-Base offers a lower-parameter alternative with competitive performance.
papers.selection_reason: Demonstrates efficient feature distillation for geospatial foundation models, significantly reducing compute costs while maintaining or improving accuracy. This addresses both spatial intelligence (geospatial understanding) and efficient AI (distillation).
papers.title: Reuse, Don't Retrain: Efficient, Modality-Versatile Geospatial Foundation Models through Feature Distillation
papers.tldr: Feature distillation efficiently repurposes geospatial foundation models into smaller, multimodal models that match or outperform larger pretrained counterparts at much lower cost.

papers.abstract: Large language models serve applications with diverse inference budgets, but training and maintaining separate models for each budget incurs substantial costs. Recent Looped Transformers enable flexible inference computation through parameter reuse, but maintaining strong performance across different inference budgets remains an open challenge. We introduce Accordion, a mixture-of-experts-based model that supports five inference budgets through fixed-prefix layer looping. Each budget follows a pre-defined execution path, while the minimum budget retains the unlooped model. Joint pretraining samples one budget per micro-batch and optimizes its next-token prediction loss without additional cross-budget consistency objectives. We further preserve these inference budgets through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, where parameter-group merging and budget-matched multi-teacher on-policy distillation integrate three domain experts into one model. After 3.6T tokens of pretraining, increasing inference depth improves Accordion-6B-A0.5B's five-category macro-average across 37 tasks by 3.01 percentage points, with the middle budget capturing 89% of this gain using half as many additional layer executions. The final model surpasses each domain expert on its corresponding task-and-budget average, while achieving strong instruction-following performance across all budgets and retaining depth-dependent gains in mathematical reasoning and code generation.
authors: Yudong Zhang, Wei Ding, Kaili Zheng, Yuchen Ding, Zhenyu Zhang
bullets: Addresses the cost of maintaining separate models for different inference budgets.
Uses fixed-prefix layer looping, with each budget following a predefined path and the minimum budget using the unlooped model.
Joint pretraining samples one budget per micro-batch and optimizes next-token prediction without cross-budget consistency losses.
Preserves budget flexibility through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with parameter-group merging and budget-matched multi-teacher distillation.

Across 37 tasks, deeper inference improves macro-average performance by 3.01 points; the middle budget captures 89% of the gain with half the extra layer executions, while gains persist in math and code.
papers.selection_reason: MoE LLM with elastic-depth inference via layer looping; relevant to LLM architectures and efficient inference.
papers.title: Accordion: Elastic-Depth Inference via Fixed-Prefix Layer Looping
papers.tldr: Accordion enables one MoE language model to trade inference cost for quality across five fixed computation budgets, with deeper execution improving performance.

papers.abstract: Deploying Vision-Language Models for video anomaly detection confronts a fundamental constraint. Their semantic reasoning demands computational budgets incompatible with the scale of real-world video streams. We present Signal-Aware Adaptive Fusion (SAAF), a framework that achieves efficient zero-shot anomaly detection through three key innovations. First, we introduce a dual-signal adaptive sampler operating in semantic embedding space: a delta signal captures sudden events via frame-to-frame cosine distance, while a drift signal detects static and gradual anomalies through deviation from rolling temporal context. Their OR-gated combination with adaptive EMA-based thresholding provides comprehensive anomaly coverage without training data. Second, we propose a threshold-gated cascaded architecture where lightweight frame-level scoring precedes expensive video-level temporal analysis, invoking it only when confidence warrants additional context. Third, we design a signal-aware weighted fusion mechanism that dynamically adapts score combination based on which signal triggered frame selection. Across four benchmarks, SAAF delivers competitive accuracy at substantially lower cost. Among training-free zero-shot methods, SAAF sets a new state of the art on XD-Violence (92.07%), MSAD (86.70%), and ShanghaiTech (80.54%) AUC-ROC, with XD-Violence and MSAD also surpassing supervised baselines. SAAF sustains 44.95, 48.61, and 41.06 FPS on XD-Violence, UCF-Crime, and MSAD, a 2.43$\times$, 2.63$\times$, and 2.22$\times$ throughput improvement over the prior best zero-shot method. Code: https://github.com/kdawoud91/SAAF
authors: Khaled Waleed Dawoud, Muhammad Haris Khan
bullets: Uses frame-to-frame semantic changes (delta) and temporal-context deviations (drift) to detect sudden, static, and gradual anomalies without training data.
Employs EMA-based adaptive thresholds and OR-gated sampling for broad anomaly coverage.
Cascades lightweight frame scoring before expensive video-level analysis, reducing unnecessary computation.
Dynamically fuses scores according to the signal that triggered frame selection.
Achieves competitive accuracy across four benchmarks and reports 2.22×–2.63× throughput gains over the prior best zero-shot method on three datasets.
papers.selection_reason: Presents an efficient zero-shot video anomaly detection framework using VLMs. It fits Video Understanding and Efficient AI (throughput improvements).
papers.title: Efficient Zero-Shot Video Anomaly Detection via Signal-Aware Adaptive Fusion (SAAF)
papers.tldr: SAAF enables efficient zero-shot video anomaly detection by adaptively sampling informative frames and selectively applying costly temporal reasoning.

papers.abstract: Adversarial sharpness penalty per iteration of a base optimizer, known as sharpness-aware minimization (SAM), is an accepted technique to improve generalization in deep learning. Recently, Muon has emerged as a dominant optimization algorithm for training large language models (LLMs). It achieves lower sample complexity for heavy-tailed gradient updates - a phenomenon common in LLM training. However, sharpness penalties with Muon updates are yet largely unexplored in the literature. Moreover, the behavior of SAM under heavy-tailed noise is unknown both theoretically and empirically. A potential reason for this gap is the additional cost of extra gradient computation per iteration for penalty perturbations in SAM, which becomes prohibitive for LLMs. This paper introduces Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithm (SOMA) to combine a computationally efficient and theoretically grounded perturbation scheme with the Muon algorithm. The key idea is to use stale (purely) stochastic gradient noise for adversarial perturbations. Theoretically, we show that SOMA's sample complexity is invariant to the perturbation direction. We provide explorations and insights into SOMA's robustness to heavy-tailed gradient noise. We extensively explore SOMA's efficacy in (a) mitigating quality degradation due to post-training quantization, and (b) catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning of LLMs.
authors: Geetika, Shivani Singh Chauhan, Gauranshi Gupta, Anant Jain, Kaushik Kalyanaraman, Bapi Chatterjee
bullets: Addresses the unexplored interaction between sharpness penalties, Muon optimization, and heavy-tailed gradient noise.
Uses stale stochastic gradient noise for adversarial perturbations, avoiding SAM’s additional gradient computation.
Provides a theoretical result showing sample complexity is invariant to the perturbation direction.
Explores robustness under heavy-tailed noise and evaluates mitigation of post-training quantization degradation and catastrophic forgetting during LLM fine-tuning.
papers.selection_reason: Computationally efficient sharpness-aware optimization for LLMs; reduces extra gradient computation and addresses forgetting/quantization.
papers.title: Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithms
papers.tldr: SOMA combines sharpness-aware perturbations with Muon using stale stochastic gradient noise to improve robustness in efficient LLM training.
