Assigns higher precision to salient key pairs once during prefill and reuses the allocation during decoding.
At 2.26-bit average precision, matches or outperforms prior mixed-precision methods using 2.32–2.39 bits across reasoning, code-generation, and AIME benchmarks.
Degrades more gracefully to 1.5 bits than compared baselines, which show sharper drops below 2.25 bits.
papers.selection_reason: Mixed-precision KV cache quantization for efficient LLM inference.
papers.title: PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference
papers.tldr: PN-Mix improves low-bit KV-cache efficiency by assigning precision using query–key pair-norm saliency, enabling strong long-output LLM accuracy at very low bit rates.

papers.abstract: Block-diffusion language models denoise a whole block of token positions in parallel so each forward pass can emit many tokens. However, blocks are still denoised in strict sequence, a cost that within-block acceleration leaves untouched. Here, we investigate decoding blocks concurrently and propose One Block Ahead (OBA), a training-free decoding algorithm that denoises the next block alongside the current one. We demonstrate that for uniform-state diffusion LMs, where a block's denoising progress is not visible in its intermediate tokens, concurrent decoding is advantageous if the next block's tokens are promoted together with the corresponding sampler state, including the self-conditioning signal and the denoising time. We also derive a break-even criterion that relates the benefit of OBA to the relative cost of a paired-block forward pass. On DiffusionGemma, a state-of-the-art diffusion LM, OBA increases the tokens per forward pass by 42.3% (from 15.64 to 22.25) and the single-request denoising throughput by 16.3%, averaged over ten benchmarks, with a small accuracy regression.
authors: Yangyi Shen, Pin-Jui Ku, Nicolai Oswald, Jean-Marie Lemercier, Yonggan Fu, Stefano Ermon, Jure Leskovec, Boris Ginsburg, Ante Juki\'c
bullets: Block-diffusion LMs generate tokens in parallel within blocks but traditionally denoise blocks sequentially.
OBA is a training-free decoder that advances the next block alongside the current block.
For uniform-state diffusion LMs, effective promotion requires carrying the next block’s sampler state, including self-conditioning and denoising time.
A break-even criterion relates OBA’s benefit to the cost of paired-block forward passes.
On DiffusionGemma, OBA raises tokens per forward pass by 42.3% and single-request denoising throughput by 16.3% across ten benchmarks, with a small accuracy regression.
papers.selection_reason: Concurrent decoding for diffusion LMs improves throughput; fits efficient inference.
papers.title: One Block Ahead: Promoting Sampler State in Diffusion Language Models
papers.tldr: One Block Ahead (OBA) accelerates block-diffusion language model decoding by denoising the next block concurrently with the current one, improving throughput with a small accuracy trade-off.

papers.abstract: MLLM-based detectors formulate vision-language grounding as autoregressive coordinate generation, yet in dense scenes, they often collapse into a box repetition loop, repeatedly emitting identical boxes until the decoding budget is exhausted. We trace this failure to historical-answer attention takeover: Under full-history autoregression, repeated coordinate tokens in the growing answer history attract disproportionate attention, crowding out the attention sinks needed to attend to new visual evidence. % To break this loop, in this paper, we propose \textbf{Compressed Window Auto-Regression} (WinAR). This new mechanism partitions a long answer sequence into consecutive generation windows and restricts full token-level autoregression to the current window only while compressing each previous window into a fixed set of latent tokens that condition subsequent decoding. This design reduces the repeated exposure to raw historical coordinates that triggers the attention takeover, yet preserves cross-window dependencies essential for coherent multi-object generation. On RSDense, which contains 200-2,000 objects per image, our model WinARDet improves RexOmni F1-score (IoU=0.5) from 32.16 to 39.36 over the baseline, while reducing the redundancy rate from 35.48% to 13.00%. WinARDet also generalizes across decoding strategies and output formats, including parallel box decoding and polygon generation, providing a practical paradigm for long-horizon vision-language grounding across scene densities.
authors: Chenxu Wang, Hangyi Kuang, Bo-Wen Yin, Yuxuan Li, Quan-Sheng Zeng, Yang Zhang, Xu Guo, Xiang Li, Qibin Hou
bullets: Dense-scene autoregressive detectors can repeatedly emit identical boxes until the decoding budget is exhausted.
The proposed Compressed Window Auto-Regression limits token-level attention to the current generation window.
Each previous window is compressed into fixed latent tokens, preserving cross-window dependencies while reducing historical-coordinate interference.
On RSDense, WinARDet raises F1 at IoU 0.5 from 32.16 to 39.36 and lowers redundancy from 35.48% to 13.00%.
The approach also extends to parallel box decoding and polygon generation across varying scene densities.
papers.selection_reason: Novel compressed window autoregression for MLLM-based dense vision-language grounding, relevant to multimodal LLMs and token efficiency.
papers.title: WinARDet: Compressed Window Auto-Regression for Long-Horizon Vision-Language Grounding
papers.tldr: WinARDet prevents repetitive box-generation loops in dense-scene vision-language grounding by compressing past decoding windows into latent tokens.

papers.abstract: Robotic ultrasound can standardize image acquisition and reduce operator workload and variability, but policy learning remains limited by the lack of realistic, controllable simulation environments. While controllable world models have advanced rapidly in natural-image domains, ultrasound world modeling remains challenging because each frame captures only a cross-section of unobserved 3D anatomy, causing small probe motions to induce large appearance changes. Existing approaches rely on robot-tracked poses and latent-space prediction, but do not directly generate the observations required for interactive control. We propose SonoWorld, a causal ultrasound world model that learns video dynamics from unlabeled clinical videos and grounds them to 6-DoF control using a small set of freehand clinical scans tracked with an EM sensor. SonoWorld is trained in three stages: pretraining a latent-action-conditioned video diffusion model on around 6.9 million unlabeled multi-organ ultrasound frames; grounding the learned video dynamics to metric probe poses with a small EM-tracked thyroid dataset; and applying distribution matching distillation to enable causal, long-horizon autoregressive generation with selectively caching eviction tokens at inference time. We evaluate controllability through pose-following fidelity, round-trip consistency, and axis-specific control under synthetic actions on held-out tracked scans, and further validate it with a user study. In model-based action discrimination, SonoWorld correctly ranks the target-directed probe motion over an equal-magnitude opposite motion in up to 74.8% of trials. To our knowledge, SonoWorld is the first causal, pose-controllable ultrasound world model learned primarily from freehand clinical videos, providing a data-driven interactive environment for robotic ultrasound data acquisition and policy evaluation.
authors: Zefan Yang, Zheyuan Zhang, Boris Maihe, Yikang Liu, Hang Yu, Ankush Mukherjee, Xiao Chen, Pingkun Yan, Terrence Chen, Shanhui Sun
bullets: Addresses the lack of realistic, controllable simulation environments for robotic ultrasound, where small probe motions can cause large image changes.
Learns video dynamics from about 6.9 million unlabeled multi-organ ultrasound frames and grounds them to 6-DoF probe poses using a small EM-tracked thyroid dataset.
Uses staged training with latent-action-conditioned video diffusion, pose grounding, and distribution-matching distillation for causal long-horizon generation.
Evaluated pose-following, round-trip consistency, axis-specific control, and user-study performance on held-out tracked scans.
Correctly ranked target-directed motion over equal-magnitude opposite motion in up to 74.8% of trials.
papers.selection_reason: Pose-controllable ultrasound world model with latent actions and token eviction, directly relevant to interactive world models.
papers.title: SonoWorld: Towards Interactive Pose-Controllable Ultrasound World Models
papers.tldr: SonoWorld is a causal ultrasound world model that generates pose-controllable video for interactive robotic ultrasound simulation and policy evaluation.

papers.abstract: One-step diffusion distillation achieves strong performance on small datasets but remains insufficient for high-resolution or complex text-to-image settings. Extending to multistep distillation often requires training data, suffers from early-step degradation, inconsistent outputs across sampling budgets, and incurs high computational cost. We identify that these limitations stem from simultaneous training, where a single adapted network approximates multiple score functions of different student distributions at once, causing biased distribution matching and unstable optimization. Therefore, we propose Progressive Multistep Data-free Distillation (PMDD), which assigns a dedicated adapted network per student distribution while avoiding the memory overhead of maintaining multiple adapted networks. Combined with a stage-wise unforget loss to preserve earlier-step generations, PMDD reduces optimization bias in the student, provides faster convergence, and a single unified model that supports multiple inference budgets. Extensive experiments show that PMDD matches or outperforms data-free few-step baselines at every multistep budget, reaches FID 1.99 on ImageNet 64x64 in two steps, below its 512-NFE teacher (2.32), and achieves FID 7.76 on zero-shot COCO 512x512, while requiring 4-5x less training compute than data-free DMDv2 to support three inference budgets.
authors: Ngoc Duy Tran, Kien Do, Duc Thanh Nguyen, Truyen Tran
bullets: Multistep distillation is challenging for high-resolution and complex text-to-image generation because it can require data, degrade early steps, produce inconsistent budgets, and be computationally expensive.
PMDD assigns a dedicated adapted network to each student distribution without retaining all networks simultaneously, reducing optimization bias.
A stage-wise unforget loss preserves earlier-step generations during progressive training.
The unified model matches or exceeds data-free few-step baselines across budgets, reaching FID 1.99 on ImageNet 64×64 in two steps and 7.76 on zero-shot COCO 512×512.
It uses 4–5× less training compute than data-free DMDv2 when supporting three inference budgets.
papers.selection_reason: Data-free multistep diffusion distillation reduces training and inference compute, relevant to efficient AI.
papers.title: Data-free Multistep Diffusion Distillation
papers.tldr: PMDD enables efficient data-free multistep diffusion distillation by progressively reducing distribution-matching bias while supporting multiple sampling budgets in one model.

papers.abstract: Transformers are intuitively considered to be efficient at copying from their inputs. We actually show that the ability of LLMs to copy in context can be improved through explicit modeling. We propose Copy-Paste Language Models (CPLMs), which add a lightweight Copy-Paste head to the conventional language modeling (LM) head. CPLMs improve training efficiency, downstream performance, and offer new operating points in long-context and retrieval setups. We validate our approach by pretraining models from 135M to 1.7B parameters, showing improvements across all scales and backbones with negligible training and inference overheads. We explain the success of CPLMs by showing that they partially mitigate the LM head gradient bottleneck through an alternative gradient path.
bullets: Transformers may copy from inputs inefficiently despite appearing naturally suited to copying.
CPLMs augment the standard language-modeling head with a lightweight Copy-Paste head.
The method improves training efficiency, downstream performance, and provides useful operating points for long-context and retrieval tasks.
Improvements hold across model scales from 135M to 1.7B parameters and across backbones, with negligible training and inference overhead.
The authors attribute the gains to an alternative gradient path that partially alleviates the LM-head gradient bottleneck.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a Copy-Paste head to explicitly model input copying in LLMs, improving training efficiency and long-context performance, which is relevant to LLM architectures and efficient attention.
papers.title: Copy-Paste Language Models
papers.tldr: Copy-Paste Language Models add a lightweight copy mechanism that improves in-context copying, efficiency, and downstream performance with negligible overhead.

papers.abstract: Large language models impose substantial memory demands and arithmetic costs during inference. Dense-to-mixture-of-experts (MoE) conversion is a model optimization technique that aims to reduce these arithmetic costs. Dense-to-MoE conversion partitions pretrained feed-forward network (FFN) neurons into experts and selects a subset for each token. Leading methods fall into two categories: analytic methods produce a converted model quickly using heuristics, while learning methods produce a model much more slowly by optimizing via gradients. Both approaches, however, fix the same active expert count, or "utilization," at every layer. We introduce Spectral-MoE, which learns to allocate a utilization budget heterogeneously across layers. Its name draws a metaphor between separating a dense FFN into experts and separating a light beam into its spectrum. Spectral-MoE consists of two distinct approaches: a static approach that uses a single per-layer scalar which is shared across tokens, and a dynamic approach which emits a per-token schedule. We demonstrate that both allocators improve performance over uniform on both the analytic-based and learning-based SOTA dense-to-MoE methods. At 25% FFN utilization, dynamic allocation reduces WikiText-2 perplexity relative to uniform by 1.04, 2.96, and 2.71 points on the learned base for Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B, respectively. The corresponding reductions on the analytic base are 2.45, 6.26, and 2.17 points. On the learned base, dynamic allocation improves six-task mean accuracy over uniform by an average of 1.5, 4.2, and 3.6 percentage points across the three models at FFN utilizations of 12.5%, 25%, and 50%, respectively. These results establish per-layer expert utilization as a novel optimization axis in dense-to-MoE conversion.
authors: Zachary Broveak, Christian Kubicka, Thierry Tambe
bullets: Addresses the inefficiency of fixed per-layer expert utilization in dense-to-MoE conversion.
Introduces static per-layer allocation shared across tokens and dynamic per-token allocation schedules.
Both approaches improve analytic- and learning-based conversion methods over uniform utilization.
At 25% FFN utilization, dynamic allocation lowers WikiText-2 perplexity by 1.04–6.26 points across the evaluated models and bases.
Dynamic allocation also improves six-task mean accuracy by 1.5–4.2 percentage points on the learned bases across tested utilization levels.
papers.selection_reason: Dense-to-MoE conversion reduces LLM inference cost; per-layer utilization is a novel optimization axis.
papers.title: Spectral-MoE: Heterogeneous Per-Layer Expert Utilization in Dense-to-MoE Conversion
papers.tldr: Spectral-MoE improves dense-to-MoE conversion by allocating different expert-utilization budgets across layers instead of using one uniform count.

papers.abstract: Transformers are efficient to pre-train at scale because attention permits parallel computation across sequence positions, but long-context inference requires increasingly large KV caches. Efficient recurrent alternatives reduce the asymptotic complexity of inference, but their sequential dependence limits token-wise parallelism during training, making them harder to scale. Further, the current paradigm of extending long context tasks creates competing notions of retaining information precisely and keeping long-context inference efficient. To address this gap, we introduce Titan-Llama, a post-training method for retrofitting attention-based language models with a hierarchical memory architecture that updates parameters at test-time. Titan-Llama applies a blockwise attention mask and preserves full-fidelity attention over recent tokens while compressing historical context into recurrent, fixed-size neural memory modules (NMMs). Our formulation allows pre-trained attention layers to be replaced without training a new language model from scratch. On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, Titan-Llama raises accuracy over segmented attention windows from 23.87\% to 40.51\% on QuALITY and from 14.50\% to 40.75\% on LongHealth. Inference benchmarks show more than 20\% faster prefill, 37\% faster decode at medium context lengths, and 24\% lower steady-state decode memory usage in the evaluated configurations. Together, these results demonstrate that incorporating memory architecture mechanisms that utilize test-time training effectively modulates long-context behavior of pre-trained models, offering a practical route to adapting pre-trained transformers for efficient long-context inference. Our code is released on Github \href{https://github.com/sarahpannn/titans-pytorch/tree/main}{GitHub}
bullets: Addresses the tension between precise information retention and efficient long-context inference.
Uses hierarchical neural memory modules, blockwise attention, and full attention over recent tokens while compressing older context into fixed-size memory.
Replaces attention layers post-training, avoiding training a new language model from scratch.
On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, improves QuALITY and LongHealth accuracy over segmented attention windows and reports faster prefill/decode with lower steady-state decode memory.
Evaluated configurations show benefits at medium context lengths; broader scope beyond the reported model and tasks is not established by the abstract.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a hierarchical memory architecture (NMMs) for retrofitting LLMs to improve long-context inference efficiency and memory usage, directly addressing LLM memory and efficiency.
papers.title: Titan-Llama: Retrofitting Pre-trained LLMs with External Neural Memory Modules
papers.tldr: Titan-Llama retrofits pretrained transformers with recurrent test-time neural memory to improve long-context accuracy while reducing inference cost.

papers.abstract: While work on LLM-based regression has largely focused on scalar prediction, multi-output text regression remains less explored. We present DualView, a parameter-efficient approach to leverage LLMs for multi-output text regression. \method{} first extracts broad and output-specific representations from a frozen LLM, then uses a dual-branch architecture to produce the full score vector. Across five heterogeneous regression tasks and eight LLMs (up to 122B), DualView outperforms seven supervised regression baselines while requiring 82--1842 times fewer fitted parameters than the three strongest baselines. These improvements extend across individual output dimensions and persist even with limited training data. Notably, DualView using a smaller open-weight LLM can outperform unsupervised prediction with Gemini 3.1 Pro. Controlled ablations show that broad and output-specific evidence provide complementary predictive benefits, while lightweight shared predictors achieve strong performance with fewer trainable parameters.
authors: Yiheng Su, Junyi Jessy Li, Matthew Lease
bullets: Addresses the underexplored problem of predicting multiple regression outputs from text with LLMs.
Extracts broad and output-specific representations, then combines them through a dual-branch architecture.
Evaluated across five heterogeneous tasks and eight LLMs, including models up to 122B parameters.
Outperforms seven supervised baselines while fitting substantially fewer parameters; gains persist with limited training data.
Ablations show complementary value from both evidence types and effective lightweight shared predictors.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a parameter-efficient dual-branch architecture for multi-output text regression, which is a relevant methodological contribution to LLM architectures and efficiency.
papers.title: DUALVIEW: Leveraging Broad and Output-Specific Evidence for LLM-based Multi-Output Text Regression
papers.tldr: DualView enables parameter-efficient multi-output text regression by combining broad and output-specific evidence from a frozen LLM.

papers.abstract: Scientific imaging data involving medical (e.g., 3D radiographic, microscopic images) and astronomical sensors pose different challenges from natural images. One key challenge is that these datasets are often orders of magnitude larger than natural images. Efficient training and inference on such data is challenging due to the increased hardware requirements, often needing bespoke solutions. Moreover, the relevant objects such as tumors and astronomical phenomena are sparsely distributed with respect to the background information. Standard efficiency techniques like quantization and pruning apply uniform scaling of all regions, potentially compromising the precision/fidelity of predictions. Thus, efficient methods that reduce computational requirements without losing resolution for relevant parts of the data and with uncertainty estimates on predictions are essential. We present \textit{Conformal Adaptation} with risk guarantees for uncertainty-aware sparse computations. Our formalism is general, spanning dense pixel-level classification and regression tasks where hierarchical models predict at low resolution, certify the signal using conformal risk control, and refine the certified predictions. We benchmark our method on multiple tasks such as 3D medical image segmentation, 2D galaxy flux prediction, and 1D calcium spike rate prediction, achieving $2.5$--$72\times$ wall-clock speedup across the various tasks, including on commodity CPUs.
authors: Shehtab Zaman, Aneesh Rangnekar, Nancy Lee, Harini Veeraraghavan
bullets: Targets oversized medical, astronomical, and other scientific data with sparsely distributed signals.
Uses hierarchical low-resolution prediction, conformal risk control, and selective refinement of certified regions.
Supports dense pixel-level classification and regression tasks across 3D, 2D, and 1D data.
Benchmarks report 2.5–72× wall-clock speedups, including on commodity CPUs.
Scope: focuses on reducing computation without sacrificing resolution for relevant signals or uncertainty estimates.
papers.selection_reason: Adaptive sparse computation with conformal certification reduces compute for scientific imaging; fits efficiency interest.
papers.title: Adaptive Computation with Conformal Certification
papers.tldr: Conformal Adaptation enables uncertainty-certified sparse computation for large scientific imaging tasks, achieving 2.5–72× wall-clock speedups while preserving refinement of relevant regions.

papers.abstract: Tokenization is an essential preprocessing step in almost all large language models (LLMs). One of the most popular frameworks is BPE tokenization, which consists of special token segmentation, pretokenization, and byte-pair encoding (BPE). However, existing algorithms are sequential, with each stage only processing complete output from the previous stage. In order to reduce latency and memory footprints, recent works (Jiang and Gong, ICML 2026) (Li, Yang and Mamouras, ASPLOS 2026) (Mamouras, Li and Yang, PLDI 2026) have initiated the study of online algorithms for subroutines such as pretokenization and BPE with a goal of streaming input to output as the input arrives online. However, the search for efficient online tokenization remains open. In this work, we formalize and resolve online tokenization. We introduce the notion of delay for online tokenization which characterizes the extent to which the algorithm output lags behind the (possibly computationally intractable) optimum. We give a near-linear time algorithm with optimal delay (up to constant factors). We complement this algorithm with a conditional lower bound: unless $\mathbf{P} = \mathbf{NP}$, there is no polynomial time algorithm that beats the delay of our algorithm by more than a constant factor. We implement a practical variant for tokenizers from OpenAI's tiktoken and HuggingFace's tokenizers. We obtain a $7.9\times$-$34.8\times$ latency advantage (measured as time to first token) over tiktoken (as well as the recent gigatoken tokenizer) and our implementation maintains approximately constant memory usage independent of input size. Our implementation also achieves a $2.4\times$-$7.0\times$ improvement in throughput over tiktoken and $15.8\times$-$38.1\times$ over tokenizers.
bullets: Defines delay for online tokenization relative to an offline optimum, even when computing that optimum may be intractable.
Provides a near-linear-time online algorithm whose delay is optimal up to constant factors.
Shows conditionally that, unless P = NP, no polynomial-time algorithm can improve its delay by more than a constant factor.
A practical implementation for tiktoken and HuggingFace tokenizers achieves lower time-to-first-token, higher throughput, and approximately constant memory usage with respect to input size.
papers.selection_reason: Online tokenization with optimal delay improves LLM preprocessing latency/memory, fitting efficient AI methods.
papers.title: Online Tokenization with Optimal Delay in Linear Time
papers.tldr: The paper formalizes online tokenization and presents a near-linear-time algorithm with provably optimal output delay and strong practical latency and throughput gains.

papers.abstract: Structured pruning reduces LLM inference costs by removing model components to produce smaller dense models. However, existing methods can cause reasoning performance to collapse on long-form reasoning tasks such as AIME. We propose \textit{LayerTrim}, a training-free structured pruning method that identifies redundant decoder layers and selectively trims their MLP features while preserving attention and decoder depth. LayerTrim is the first training-free structured pruning method designed to preserve long-form reasoning without gradients or recovery training. Across three reasoning language models and five benchmarks, LayerTrim outperforms existing structured pruning methods in most evaluated settings, improving average accuracy by up to 21.4 percentage points over RESP. On \texttt{Qwen3-14B}, LayerTrim achieves 1.24$\times$ faster prefill and 19.7\% lower peak GPU memory than the dense model, while better preserving reasoning ability. It also achieves the shortest average generation length among evaluated pruned models, while retaining the highest average accuracy. These results demonstrate that LayerTrim improves reasoning efficiency through both structural compression and reduced token generation.
authors: Woosang Lim, Haneul Yoo, Vincent-Daniel Yun, Sungjoo Yoo
bullets: Targets reasoning degradation caused by conventional structured pruning on long-form tasks such as AIME.
Identifies redundant decoder layers and selectively trims their MLP features without gradients or recovery training.
Evaluated across three reasoning language models and five benchmarks, outperforming existing pruning methods in most settings.
Improves average accuracy by up to 21.4 percentage points over RESP.
On Qwen3-14B, delivers 1.24× faster prefill and 19.7% lower peak GPU memory than the dense model while preserving reasoning ability.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a training-free structured pruning method (LayerTrim) for LLMs that preserves reasoning ability, addressing efficiency and performance trade-offs.
papers.title: Unlocking Structured Pruning for Reasoning Language Models via Attention-Preserving MLP Trimming
papers.tldr: LayerTrim is a training-free structured pruning method that reduces reasoning-model inference costs while preserving long-form reasoning by trimming MLP features and retaining attention and decoder depth.

papers.abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) applies every rank-one component of its update to every token, and mixture-of-experts variants replace this with a learned router that activates a fixed number of components. We argue that the number of components a token needs is a detection question with a classical answer. A token's responses to the rank-one components of a trained LoRA consist of a few large values on a Gaussian noise floor whose width matches that of an untrained adapter, and the floor carries cross-talk rather than adaptation. We introduce SQUELCH, a router-free mixture of rank-one experts that (i) soft-thresholds each token's responses at a multiple of its own robust noise level, so the active rank varies per token; (ii) chooses that multiple for each module by Stein's unbiased risk estimate, so no rank budget is specified; and (iii) replaces the resulting marginal keep-or-drop decisions by one explaining-away step on the value Gram matrix, which suppresses redundant co-active components and recruits complementary ones. SQUELCH adds no trainable parameters to LoRA. We prove that the squelch is within a logarithmic factor of the oracle input-dependent allocation, that the selected threshold is risk-consistent, and that explaining away is a descent step toward the joint sparse code whose error is controlled by the coherence of co-active components. On commonsense reasoning, knowledge, math, code, and GLUE with LLaMA-3.1-8B, Qwen3, and DeBERTaV3, SQUELCH improves over LoRA by 2.2--3.2 points and over the strongest mixture baseline by 0.8--1.2 points while activating 8.6 of 32 components per token on average.
authors: Mei Okonkwo, Owen Castellanos, Ingrid Solberg, Yusuf Demirel
bullets: Motivation: LoRA applies every rank-one component to every token, although many responses appear to be cross-talk on a Gaussian noise floor.
Method: A router-free mechanism estimates each token’s robust noise level and soft-thresholds component responses, allowing the active rank to vary without a preset rank budget.
Thresholds are chosen per module using Stein’s unbiased risk estimate; an explaining-away step suppresses redundant components and favors complementary ones.
Theory: The method is near-optimal up to a logarithmic factor, has risk-consistent threshold selection, and provides coherence-based error control for joint sparse coding.
Experiments across reasoning, knowledge, math, code, and GLUE tasks report gains over LoRA and a mixture baseline while activating 8.6 of 32 components per token on average.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces SQUELCH, a router-free method for efficient token-level adaptation in LoRA, improving efficiency and performance in LLMs through noise-floor squelching and explaining-away mechanisms.
papers.title: How Many Ranks Does a Token Need? A Noise-Floor Squelch for Rank-One LoRA Experts
papers.tldr: SQUELCH dynamically selects only the rank-one LoRA components each token needs by thresholding noise and removing redundancy, improving performance while using fewer components.

papers.abstract: Sparse attention reduces the KV-cache traffic that dominates long-context LLM decoding, but practical methods largely operate at coarse granularity. Token-level selection offers finer control, yet presents two challenges: low-dimensional scoring may lose query--key structure needed for accurate ranking, while gathering scattered selected tokens can offset the resulting latency benefit. We introduce Joint Subspace Sparse Attention (JSSA) to address both challenges. For selection quality, JSSA learns a shared low-dimensional query--key subspace by minimizing token-score preservation error. We upper-bound the resulting non-convex objective with a tractable marginal objective that admits a closed-form spectral solution; direct refinement of the exact objective provides no measurable improvement in the tested settings. For execution efficiency, we develop a gather-free token-level indexed-attention kernel that supports distinct per-KV-head selections under the standard grouped-query attention (GQA) KV-cache layout. Across standard GQA, hybrid sliding-window/global attention, and Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) models, JSSA consistently remains close to full-KV accuracy while avoiding the substantial generation-length inflation and architecture-dependent failures observed with competing methods. On an NVIDIA B200 GPU, JSSA achieves up to $6.43\times$ the decoding throughput of full-KV attention at 128K context. JSSA achieves reasoning accuracy comparable to model-native DSA without model training and reaches 96--99\% of its decoding throughput even at 700B scale large models.
authors: Jiwon Song, Yoongon Kim, Jae-Joon Kim
bullets: Addresses low-dimensional token-ranking errors and the latency cost of gathering scattered KV-cache tokens.
Learns a shared query–key subspace via a tractable spectral objective for token selection.
Introduces a gather-free indexed-attention kernel supporting distinct selections per KV head under GQA.
Remains close to full-KV accuracy across GQA, hybrid sliding-window/global attention, and MLA models.
Matches model-native DSA reasoning accuracy without training and reaches 96–99% of its decoding throughput at 700B scale.
papers.selection_reason: Sparse attention for efficient long-context decoding; directly relevant to efficient attention and KV-cache reduction.
papers.title: Joint Subspace Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Decoding
papers.tldr: JSSA enables accurate, token-level sparse attention for long-context decoding while reducing KV-cache traffic and achieving up to 6.43× full-KV throughput at 128K context.

papers.abstract: Summary-token architectures such as Kwai Summary Attention (KSA) compress distant context into learnable Summary token per chunk, and hybrid variants interleave these layers with full attention to retain exact access to the original text. In such hybrid KSA-Full architecture, the interleaving inserted summary tokens are served as a streaming flow role across different layers. Although effective, however, it also introduce some bottlenecks: (1) the different layers summary compression chunk must be same, therefore hard to reach a flexible KV Cache compression, e.g., different layer set different summary compression chunk window. (2) in the full-attention layers, the summary token introduced additional computation cost, but such layer ignore them and still pay quadratic prefilling, therefore unfriendly to the computation side. Motivated by them, we developed the KSA V2, which not only achieves a more flexible KV cache memory compression but also reduces the computation cost in Full attention layer. Specifically, we found that the summary tokens can serve two roles: the KV memory and sparse indexer.
authors: OneRec Team, Chenglong Chu, Guohong Mu, Guowang Zhang, Hao Peng, Hui Wang, Jian Liang, Jiangxia Cao, Jiao Ou, Jiaxin Deng, Lu Ren, Muhao Wei, Ruiming Tang, Tianle Xu, Wenwu Ou, Xingmei Wang, Zhixin Ling, Zhiyuan Liang, Ziqi Wang, Chaoyi Ma, Haixiao Gao, Kuo Cai, Renpu Liu, Ruochen Yang, Wenlong Xu, Xinqi Jin, Yan Sun, Yifan Wang, Yingzhi He, Yiyu Wang, Yusen Huo, Zhaojie Liu, Zihan Zhou
bullets: Addresses fixed summary-compression windows across layers, which limit flexible KV-cache compression.
Reduces wasted computation in full-attention layers that previously ignored summary tokens while still incurring quadratic prefilling cost.
Uses summary tokens in two roles: compressed KV memory and sparse indexing.
Targets both more flexible KV-cache memory compression and lower full-attention computation cost.
papers.selection_reason: Summary-token attention with flexible KV cache compression and reduced full-attention cost; fits efficient AI and long-context LLM methods.
papers.title: Kwai Summary Attention V2 Technical Report
papers.tldr: KSA V2 makes hybrid summary-token attention more flexible and efficient by separating summary tokens’ KV-memory and sparse-indexing roles.

papers.abstract: Layer-wise post-training quantization methods let each layer compensate for the quantization error inherited from earlier layers. We ask under what assumptions such compensation guarantees a network output error no larger than without it. For linear networks of any depth, with the required calibration Gram matrices invertible, if the rounding error of each layer has zero conditional mean and a deterministic second-moment map common to both schemes, as under subtractive dither on an unbounded grid, then compensation with strengths in $[0,1]$ fixed in advance gives a mean-square output error no larger than no compensation, each scheme being followed along its own trajectory. The exact gain separates error removed directly from reduced excitation of later rounding noise. Outside this setting the comparison can fail. With rectified linear activations it fails for two independent reasons: noise changes activation states, and, even when no state changes, the correction moves error from samples on which a unit is inactive to samples on which it is active. With stable activations, commutators between the calibration projection and the activation patterns bound the excess. With a bounded codebook, even unique exact layer-wise minimizers with no overload can give a larger output error. For fixed rounding errors it already fails for two scalar linear layers, refuting a published universal guarantee. An exact residual identity gives the necessary and sufficient condition on a common layer input. All these comparisons hold the calibration input fixed. On two 8B models at 4 bits, fixed half-strength compensation beat uncompensated rounding in every model, text and draw tested, yet no rule for choosing the strength beat a layer-wise rule consistently, and lowering the full-network loss on the data used to choose did not reliably lower it on new text.
bullets: For arbitrary-depth linear networks, fixed compensation strengths in [0,1] do not increase mean-square error when calibration Gram matrices are invertible and rounding errors satisfy suitable zero-conditional-mean and shared second-moment conditions.
The gain comes from both directly removing inherited error and reducing the excitation of later quantization noise.
Guarantees can fail with ReLU activations, bounded codebooks, or fixed rounding errors—even for two scalar linear layers; stable activations admit bounds based on projection–activation commutators.

Experiments on two 8B models at 4 bits found fixed half-strength compensation consistently better than uncompensated rounding across tested models and inputs, but no strength-selection rule was consistently best or reliably transferable to new text.
papers.selection_reason: Theoretical analysis of layer-wise post-training quantization error compensation; directly relevant to efficient AI model compression.
papers.title: When Does Compensating Inherited Quantization Error Help? Mean-Square Guarantees for Layer-Wise Quantization and Their Limits
papers.tldr: Compensating inherited quantization error is mean-square safe only under specific linear-network assumptions and can worsen output error outside them.

papers.abstract: Structured pruning reduces the inference cost of large language models (LLMs) by permanently removing neurons and weight rows, yielding dense, hardware-agnostic speedup. Existing post-training methods couple neuron selection and weight reconstruction through a shared calibration dataset, introducing domain bias and out-of-memory failures at high sparsity. We propose SARATHI, a framework that decouples these two stages. A data-free \emph{NMF Residual Subspace Probe} scores neurons using intrinsic weight geometry, without accessing any calibration data, and carries a formal connection to Robust PCA. \emph{Adaptive OBS} then reconstructs the pruned weights with a localized calibration batch, operating in $\mathcal{O}(d^2)$ peak memory per layer and eliminating the global memory bottleneck of coupled methods. A \emph{Bias Shift Compensation} step corrects systematic activation drift in post-LayerNorm architectures that would otherwise cause perplexity collapse at high sparsity. Experiments across six models from two architecture families (gated and non-gated FFN) at 15--40\% sparsity show that SARATHI achieves competitive perplexity and matches or exceeds existing structured pruning baselines on zero-shot accuracy.
authors: Sankar Behera, Dhruv Singh, Satyadev Ahlawat, Yamuna Prasad
bullets: Addresses domain bias and out-of-memory failures caused by coupling pruning decisions with reconstruction on one calibration dataset.
Uses an NMF Residual Subspace Probe to score neurons from intrinsic weight geometry without calibration data.
Applies Adaptive OBS with localized calibration batches and O(d²) peak memory per layer for weight reconstruction.
Adds Bias Shift Compensation to mitigate activation drift and perplexity collapse in post-LayerNorm models.
Across six models at 15–40% sparsity, achieves competitive perplexity and matches or exceeds structured-pruning baselines on zero-shot accuracy.
papers.selection_reason: Structured LLM pruning directly targets inference cost and memory reduction, fitting Efficient AI.
papers.title: SARATHI: Decoupled Data-Free Probing and Adaptive Reconstruction for Structured LLM Pruning
papers.tldr: SARATHI enables high-sparsity structured LLM pruning by separating data-free neuron selection from memory-efficient, calibration-based weight reconstruction.

papers.abstract: KV caches make long-context serving efficient by reusing past computation, but model switching breaks this reuse and forces the receiver to prefill the context again. We study \emph{zero-prefill cross-model context handoff}: translating a sender cache into a receiver-compatible state so that the receiver can continue directly without prefilling same context. Existing affine transport methods show that receiver KV states can be substantially reconstructed from sender caches. However, through extensive analyses, we find that reconstruction fidelity is a poor proxy for receiver utility. Similar K/V reconstruction errors can lead to substantially different attention patterns, predictive distributions, and downstream accuracy, because conventional reconstruction objectives overlook the query-dependent functional importance of K and V in receiver attention. We thus introduce CACHELINK, which learns a coupled K/V correction through the receiver behavior directly. Across four independently trained sender--receiver pairs and seven evaluation panels, CACHELINK improves the equal-weight mean over all methods for every pair. In matched diagnostics, CACHELINK changes K/V squared error by less than 0.4% while substantially changing receiver attention and next-token behavior. At 32K context, it reduces handoff latency by up to $7.27\times$ relative to receiver re-prefill. Our findings verify that reconstruction fidelity alone is insufficient and that preserving the receiver computation induced by the transported cache is important for effective cross-model KV transport.
authors: Haomiao Qiu, Yining Tang, Zijia Song, Ruizi Han, Ziyue Qiao, Miao Zhang
bullets: Cross-model switching normally forces the receiver to re-prefill the shared context, reducing KV-cache reuse.
The work finds that similar K/V reconstruction errors can produce very different attention patterns, predictions, and downstream accuracy.
CacheLink learns a coupled K/V correction guided directly by receiver computation and behavior.
Across four sender–receiver pairs and seven evaluation panels, it achieved the best equal-weight mean for every pair.
At 32K context, it reduced handoff latency by up to 7.27× versus receiver re-prefill.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes functional KV cache transport for zero-prefill cross-model handoff, directly targeting inference cache efficiency.
papers.title: CacheLink: Functional KV Transport for Zero-Prefill Cross-Model Context Handoff
papers.tldr: CacheLink transports KV caches between models by optimizing receiver behavior rather than reconstruction fidelity, enabling effective zero-prefill context handoff.

papers.abstract: Recently, AutoRegressive Visual Generation (ARVG) models have emerged as a competitive paradigm for high-quality image synthesis. However, their substantial computational and memory demands make them difficult to deploy on resource-constrained edge devices. Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) provides a promising solution to reduce the computational and memory costs of ARVG models, yet existing methods often suffer from substantial image quality degradation under low-bit quantization. In this paper, we propose a training-free PTQ framework for ARVG, consisting of Tail-Aware Bounded-init Grid Refinement (T-BGR) and Coarse-to-Fine Activation Precision Scheduling (CAPS). T-BGR introduces a tail-aware reconstruction objective for weight quantizer calibration, assigning greater importance to distribution-tail coefficients and preserving fine-grained information without introducing additional parameters or high-precision branches. CAPS performs coarse-to-fine activation precision scheduling by jointly considering the importance and computational cost of different generation stages, enabling efficient mixed-precision allocation under a given bit budget. Extensive experiments on multiple ARVG backbones demonstrate that our framework consistently improves robustness under aggressive low-bit quantization. Notably, on Infinity, our framework achieves near full-precision image generation quality at an effective W4A5.6 activation precision, while existing methods at W4A6 still exhibit noticeable quality degradation or inconsistent performance. Code is available at https://github.com/lxm-lc/HGA-Quant.
authors: Xinmeng Liu, Xianglong Yan, Kaicheng Yang, Weisheng Dong, Yulun Zhang
bullets: Targets the high computational and memory costs that hinder ARVG deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.
T-BGR uses a tail-aware reconstruction objective to better preserve important weight-distribution information during quantizer calibration.
CAPS allocates mixed activation precision across generation stages based on stage importance and computational cost under a bit budget.
Experiments across multiple ARVG backbones show improved robustness to aggressive low-bit quantization.
On Infinity, it achieves near full-precision quality at effective W4A5.6 activation precision, while W4A6 existing methods show degradation or inconsistency.
papers.selection_reason: Training-free quantization framework reducing memory and compute for autoregressive visual generation models.
papers.title: HGA-Quant: Heterogeneity-Aware Quantization for AutoRegressive Visual Generation Models
papers.tldr: HGA-Quant is a training-free PTQ framework that preserves ARVG image quality under aggressive low-bit quantization through heterogeneity-aware weight calibration and activation precision scheduling.

papers.abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) are shaped by the spectral structure induced by their input encodings and activation functions. Existing methods improve fitting primarily by modifying which frequencies are available to the network, through coordinate encodings or periodic nonlinearities. However, frequency access is not the only bottleneck: signals with localized or spatially varying structure require the network to efficiently compose frequencies into multi-harmonic internal responses. We introduce learnable spectral activations (LSA), which replace fixed neuron-level nonlinearities with a residual truncated Fourier series whose harmonic amplitudes are learned during training. LSA does not expand the asymptotic function class. Instead, it changes the factorization of the representation: linear weights select features while activation coefficients control spectral shaping, and the two are updated by separate gradients. Because the activation output is affine in the coefficients given fixed pre-activations, spectral tuning becomes a more direct subproblem compared to architectures where it is entangled with feature selection. Empirically, this factorization concentrates more target-signal energy in the leading eigenmodes of the neural tangent kernel, consistent with improved optimization behavior. Across audio, image, neural radiance field, and neural acoustic field tasks, LSA also improves reconstruction quality.
bullets: Problem: Existing encodings and periodic activations expand frequency access but may struggle with localized or spatially varying structures requiring multi-harmonic composition.
Method: Replace fixed activations with residual truncated Fourier series whose harmonic amplitudes are learned during training.
Key idea: Linear weights select features while activation coefficients independently control spectral shaping, without expanding the asymptotic function class.

Result: The factorization concentrates more target-signal energy in leading neural tangent kernel eigenmodes and improves reconstruction quality across audio, image, neural radiance field, and neural acoustic field tasks.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces learnable spectral activations for implicit neural representations, relevant to 3D vision and efficient representation learning.
papers.title: Learnable Spectral Activations
papers.tldr: Learnable Spectral Activations improve implicit neural representations by learning how neurons compose frequencies, enabling better optimization and reconstruction across several signal domains.

papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards improves reasoning, while the allocation of learning signal shapes which solutions remain accessible under repeated sampling. Group-relative objectives assign equal advantages to equally rewarded responses, making aggregate credit proportional to sampled mode frequency. We introduce Exploration-Preserving Policy Optimization (ExPPO), a lightweight advantage-shaping rule that redistributes credit using prompt-relative, length-normalized response surprisal and prompt pass rate. ExPPO combines bounded shaping with shared normalization to preserve verifier polarity and approximately maintain each prompt group's total absolute sequence-advantage mass. Our analysis characterizes response-level credit allocation alongside sampled mode updates, deriving local conditions for gains in entropy and correct-mode discovery. Experiments show improved in-domain and out-of-domain reasoning coverage, higher aggregate response accuracy, and strong coverage at large sampling budgets. A controlled multi-answer evaluation further demonstrates increased correct-mode yield and gains in diversity among verified-correct responses. Code is available at https://github.com/jinhangzhan/ExPPO
bullets: Addresses group-relative objectives that can concentrate learning on frequently sampled solution modes.
Uses prompt-relative, length-normalized response surprisal and prompt pass rate to redistribute credit.
Applies bounded shaping and shared normalization to preserve verifier polarity and approximately conserve each prompt group’s absolute advantage mass.
Analysis links response-level credit allocation to entropy and correct-mode discovery.
Experiments report improved in- and out-of-domain coverage, aggregate accuracy, large-budget coverage, and diversity among verified-correct responses.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a policy optimization method for RL that preserves exploration, relevant to robot learning and efficient credit assignment.
papers.title: Exploration-Preserving Policy Optimization
papers.tldr: ExPPO reshapes reinforcement-learning advantages to preserve exploration while improving correct-solution discovery and reasoning coverage.

papers.abstract: Deep graph learning models deployed in real-world systems often need to cope with non-stationary environments, where the underlying graph distribution drifts continually over time. Prevailing solutions rely on training auxiliary generative modules to synthesize memory graphs for cross-domain adaptation, which incurs substantial computational overhead and scales poorly under prolonged distribution shifts. We argue that a more economical path exists: rather than generating memory, one can crystallize it. To this end, we propose Efficient Memory Crystallization (EMC), a training-free test-time framework that distills each incoming graph domain into a compact, semantically faithful memory through a closed-form solution to a memory-oriented distribution-matching objective, thereby eliminating redundant domain information under continual covariate shifts. To preserve both generalizability and adaptability as the model traverses a long sequence of target domains, EMC further models inter-domain dependencies through state-evolving memories and admits a theoretically grounded, tighter generalization error bound than direct adaptation. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of EMC over state-of-the-art baselines on graphs under non-stationary distribution shifts, while reducing average runtime by 87.4% and GPU memory consumption by 92.4% relative to the recent competitor, making continual graph adaptation practical at scale.
bullets: Addresses the computational and scalability costs of synthesizing memory graphs during prolonged graph distribution shifts.
Uses a training-free, test-time framework with a closed-form distribution-matching objective to distill each incoming domain into a compact, semantically faithful memory.
Models inter-domain dependencies with state-evolving memories to balance generalizability and adaptability across target domains.
Provides a theoretically tighter generalization error bound than direct adaptation.
Outperforms state-of-the-art baselines while reducing average runtime by 87.4% and GPU memory use by 92.4% relative to a recent competitor.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a test-time framework for memory crystallization in graph learning, relevant to test-time adaptation and memory efficiency.
papers.title: Efficient Memory Crystallization for Graph Learning under Non-Stationary Distribution Shifts
papers.tldr: EMC enables efficient continual graph adaptation under non-stationary distribution shifts by crystallizing compact domain memories without training generative modules.

papers.abstract: Recent work on anchored diffusion language models improves denoising by shaping an intermediate latent space with supervised important-token targets. In this work, we introduce time-based (self-supervised) anchoring, which learns and reuses latent anchors without requiring such targets. Our key observation is that anchors encode persistent properties of the clean sequence, such as its semantic intent, global structure, or intermediate plan. Although their hidden representations become stale as the token canvas evolves, their semantic content remains useful across nearby diffusion times. This is implemented through a two-stage architecture consisting of a relatively expensive anchor network that generates the latent cache state and a lightweight denoising network that intelligently combines the cached latent state with the current state at each reverse step using a fusion module. This gives anchoring a latent-space caching interpretation: the anchor network is evaluated periodically, while its cached representation is reused across multiple reverse steps. We instantiate this framework as TADM:Post-train, which time-anchorizes pretrained DLMs, and TADM:Pretraining, which learns time-based anchors during pretraining. Applied to DiffusionGemma-26B, TADM:Post-train improves throughput by approximately 49% to 79% on several math, code, and STEM benchmarks (GSM8K, AIME26, GPQA-Diamond, LiveCodeBench-v6, HumanEval, MMLU-Pro). TADM:Pretraining reduces Transformer-layer computation by up to 38% relative to a standard single-stage DLM, achieves up to 73% higher measured throughput than ADLM.
bullets: Addresses the high per-step computation of diffusion language models and the need for supervised important-token targets in prior anchored approaches.
Uses a two-stage architecture: an expensive anchor network periodically creates a latent cache, while a lightweight denoiser fuses the cache with the current state across reverse steps.
Introduces TADM:Post-train for adapting pretrained DLMs and TADM:Pretraining for learning time-based anchors during pretraining.
On DiffusionGemma-26B, TADM:Post-train improves throughput by about 49–79% across math, code, and STEM benchmarks.
TADM:Pretraining cuts Transformer-layer computation by up to 38% and reaches up to 73% higher measured throughput than ADLM.
papers.selection_reason: Time-anchored diffusion language models with latent-space caching for faster generation, relevant to efficient inference and LLM architectures.
papers.title: Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation
papers.tldr: Time-based latent anchoring caches persistent sequence information across diffusion steps, substantially accelerating diffusion language model generation without supervised anchor targets.

papers.abstract: Large-scale vision-language models (VLM) such as CLIP enable strong open-vocabulary reasoning, yet deploying these capabilities on resource-constrained edge devices remains challenging. EdgeVL addresses this problem by distilling CLIP representations into lightweight multi-modal encoders and applying quantization-aware training (QAT) for efficient Open-Vocabulary Classification (OVC) on edge hardware. However, its two-stage optimization applies different objectives for distillation and QAT, and contrastive learning is performed within the quantized student space, which can result in inconsistent optimization and reduced training efficiency. Moreover, identical supervision across RGB and non-RGB modalities may lead to modality imbalance. We propose a unified framework for quantized semantic distillation tailored to edge deployment. By jointly optimizing distillation and quantization within a unified teacher-anchored framework, our method ensures consistent training under quantization, suppressing hard negatives and enlarging decision margins. Additionally, we design a lightweight cross-attention adapter that enhances non-RGB representations through RGB-guided semantic transfer, narrowing the modality gap. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements on non-RGB modalities while maintaining deployment efficiency.
bullets: Targets the difficulty of deploying CLIP-like VLM capabilities on resource-constrained edge hardware.
Jointly optimizes semantic distillation and quantization-aware training to provide consistent learning under quantization.
Uses a lightweight cross-attention adapter for RGB-guided semantic transfer to reduce the gap between RGB and non-RGB modalities.
Suppresses hard negatives and enlarges decision margins through teacher-anchored optimization.
Experiments show consistent gains on non-RGB modalities while preserving deployment efficiency.
papers.selection_reason: Quantization-aware distillation and cross-modal alignment for edge vision-language models, directly an efficiency method.
papers.title: Efficient Quantization-Aware Distillation with Cross-Modal Alignment for Edge Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: A unified teacher-anchored distillation and quantization framework improves efficient open-vocabulary vision-language inference on edge devices, especially for non-RGB modalities.

papers.abstract: The BabyLM challenge measures how much language a model can learn from developmentally-plausible, child-scale data rather than internet-scale corpora, yet prior language models forgo the biological constraints of the neural circuitry that acquires human language: spiking neurons separated into excitatory and inhibitory populations wired by a recurrent lateral connectome. This paper presents URCHIN (Unified Recurrent Connectome with Horizontal Integrate-and-fire Neurons), which applies the Parallelized Hierarchical Connectome Spiking State-space Model (PHCSSM) to language modeling: leaky integrate-and-fire neurons coupled by a Dale's-law lateral connectome resolve each token through a multi-transmission loop that recirculates activity to a fixed point. The instantiation is deliberately minimal: a single horizontal layer of 128 neurons, no attention, and 4.23M parameters. Two implementations share one set of weights and produce identical benchmark scores, so URCHIN is trained once and deployed either way with no conversion step: a parallel state-space model (SSM) scan that is GPU-efficient for training, or an event-driven recurrent spiking neural network (RSNN) with constant-cost inference for CPU or neuromorphic edge deployment. Across all three BabyLM tracks (Strict-100M, Strict-Small, and Multilingual), URCHIN offers a biologically plausible, efficient, and directly deployable reference point.
bullets: Targets the BabyLM challenge and biologically constrained language learning.
Uses PHCSSM with leaky integrate-and-fire neurons, excitatory/inhibitory populations, and a Dale’s-law recurrent lateral connectome.
A minimal architecture with one 128-neuron horizontal layer, no attention, and 4.23M parameters.
The same weights support GPU-efficient parallel SSM training and constant-cost event-driven RSNN inference, without conversion.
Evaluated across BabyLM’s Strict-100M, Strict-Small, and Multilingual tracks as an efficient, directly deployable reference point.
papers.selection_reason: Spiking language model with constant-cost event-driven inference and dual SSM deployment, an efficiency-focused architecture.
papers.title: URCHIN: A Horizontal Spiking Language Model for Data-Constrained Pretraining
papers.tldr: URCHIN is a compact, biologically inspired spiking language model designed for efficient pretraining on child-scale data.

papers.abstract: Delayed Tensor Parallelism (DTP) removes the blocking all-reduce of tensor-parallel Transformer inference. Every device adds its own partial output to its residual stream (and broadcasts it) immediately, but only gathers (receives) the other devices' partials $δ$ modules later. A TP to DTP change therefore amounts to a real architecture change, and dense Transformer models need to be retrained or distilled after adaptation. We show that DTP breaks the permutation symmetry of neurons inside FFNs and of KV heads inside attention modules, and that this symmetry breakage makes the sharding itself a modelling decision. We show that maximising the affinity between the KV heads and the FFN neurons co-located on a device, by permuting the dense model before sharding, speeds up the distillation or retraining process. The affinity is measured with a first-order approximation of the damage that losing a head's contribution does to each neuron's output, and the co-located affinity is maximised with a coordinate-ascent optimiser that alternates an exact balanced assignment of neurons with an exhaustive search over the KV head partitions. The whole procedure takes under two minutes on one GPU for Qwen3-0.6B and Danube3-500M. On these models, at $δ=1$, the affinity-optimised layouts reach any distillation target in about half to two thirds of the steps needed by the naive contiguous layouts, over the whole 10k-step range we tested, and every optimised seed beats every contiguous seed and all but one of the sixteen random layouts. We also show that the co-located affinity score at initialisation predicts the KL to the base model after training, across seventeen layouts ranging from anti-optimised to optimised (Pearson $-0.81$ and $-0.89$).
bullets: DTP removes blocking all-reduce but changes the model architecture, requiring retraining or distillation.
DTP breaks permutation symmetry, making neuron and KV-head sharding choices important modeling decisions.
The method maximizes neuron–KV-head affinity using a first-order damage estimate and coordinate-ascent balanced assignments.
On Qwen3-0.6B and Danube3-500M, optimized layouts reached distillation targets in roughly half to two-thirds as many steps as contiguous layouts across 10k steps.
Initial affinity strongly predicted post-training KL divergence across 17 layouts, though results were evaluated on two small models and a fixed setting of δ=1.
papers.selection_reason: Optimizes sharding for delayed tensor parallelism to accelerate LLM distillation/retraining, an efficiency-oriented method for Transformer inference.
papers.title: Affinity-Aware Sharding for Delayed Tensor Parallelism
papers.tldr: Affinity-aware neuron/KV-head sharding substantially accelerates DTP adaptation by arranging co-located components to preserve their interactions.

papers.abstract: We generally perceive that training text-to-image diffusion models requires heavy compute: it is true if we aim at a comprehensive frontier model. This understanding prevents people from training their own models when getting started in the field. We develop MiniDog, a framework that enables pretraining diffusion transformers in 55 minutes and fine-tuning in another 15 minutes on four 3090 GPUs. For data, we use 26k dog images from ImageNet and caption them for pretraining and use 2k images generated by FLUX.1-schnell for fine-tuning. We precompute the image and text features and cache them for efficiency. For architecture, we use E2E-INVAE for its semantic latent space, a small transformer with 22M parameters, a small Qwen model for text encoding, and in-context conditioning. For training, we use iREPA and an EUPE perception encoder for acceleration. For evaluation, our repository supports FID, HPSv2 score, PickScore, and various VAE reconstruction metrics.
authors: Reyhaneh Esmailizadeh, Xingjian Leng, Zhanhao Liang, Liang Zheng
bullets: Targets the high compute barrier that discourages newcomers from training text-to-image models.
Uses 26k ImageNet dog images for pretraining and 2k FLUX.1-schnell-generated images for fine-tuning.
Combines cached image/text features, E2E-INVAE latents, a 22M-parameter transformer, Qwen text encoding, and in-context conditioning.
Applies iREPA and an EUPE perception encoder to accelerate training.
The framework supports FID, HPSv2, PickScore, and VAE reconstruction evaluation; the abstract does not report metric values.
papers.selection_reason: Efficient text-to-image diffusion pretraining and fine-tuning on consumer GPUs via caching and small architectures, relevant to reducing training compute.
papers.title: Dog-Breed Text-to-image Flow Matching from Pretraining to Fine-Tuning on 4 Consumer GPUs
papers.tldr: MiniDog shows that a small dog-breed text-to-image diffusion transformer can be pretrained and fine-tuned efficiently on four consumer GPUs.

papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models have advanced rapidly, but most remain optimized for single-image inputs. Multi-image reasoning is costly because each image adds many visual tokens, increasing encoding and attention demands. Existing techniques that address the above issue, including visual token pruning, token merging, visual token compression, learned resampling, hierarchical compression, retrieval-augmented visual reasoning, and memory-based architectures, have largely been designed for single-image scenarios, where redundancy is primarily spatial and local. Multi-image reasoning introduces additional challenges: redundancy may occur across images, task-relevant evidence may be sparse or distributed, and aggressive per-image compression can remove details needed for comparison, counting, temporal reasoning, retrieval, or evidence grounding. Moreover, existing token-reduction methods are often either (i) training-free but inference-inefficient, typically relying on accessing attention matrices to get token-importance that may be impractical to access with memory-efficient attention implementations such as FlashAttention, or (ii) training-dependent, requiring the base MLLM to be retrained or adapted to a new compressed-token paradigm. In this work, we study scalable multi-image reasoning and understanding without retraining the base model and without accessing attention matrices at inference time. To this end, we propose mmVB, a lightweight plug-and-play module that assigns query-conditioned per-image token budgets via cross-image context, adding only 1.6M trainable parameters while reducing visual input tokens by 9x. This reduction yields 5x faster time-to-first-token and 7x fewer prefill FLOPs, while maintaining 94.4% of full-resolution accuracy across eight multi-image reasoning benchmarks.
authors: Aimon Rahman, Joymallya Chakraborty, Vidit Bansal, Abhishek Dan
bullets: Multi-image inputs are expensive because each image contributes many visual tokens, with relevant evidence potentially sparse or distributed across images.
mmVB uses cross-image context to assign query-conditioned, per-image token budgets.
The lightweight plug-in adds 1.6M trainable parameters and reduces visual input tokens by 9×.
It delivers 5× faster time-to-first-token and 7× fewer prefill FLOPs while retaining 94.4% of full-resolution accuracy across eight benchmarks.
The approach targets multi-image reasoning without modifying or retraining the base model.
papers.selection_reason: Query-conditioned visual token budgeting for efficient multi-image MLLM reasoning, directly relevant to token pruning and multimodal LLMs.
papers.title: Visual Tokens on Demand: Visual Budgeting for Scalable and Efficient Multi-Image Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs
papers.tldr: mmVB enables efficient multi-image reasoning by dynamically allocating visual-token budgets across images without retraining the base multimodal LLM or accessing attention matrices.

papers.abstract: Pixel-space diffusion models provide an appealing alternative to latent-space diffusion models by directly modeling raw images without relying on a learned tokenizer. However, scaling pixel-space models has predominantly followed dense strategies, tightly coupling model capacity with active computation. In this work, we show that standard LLM-style Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures can be effectively transferred to pixel-space diffusion. Building on this finding, we introduce PixelMoE, a pixel-space generative framework that sparsely scales model capacity with standard LLM-style MoE, without diffusion-specific routing mechanisms or auxiliary routing objectives. Specifically, PixelMoE combines standard Token-Choice (TC) routing with fine-grained routed experts for input-adaptive sparse computation, a shared expert for capturing common representations, and a bias-based load-balancing strategy. To complement sparse capacity scaling, PixelMoE further introduces Pixel-Space Hierarchical Flow Matching, which varies spatial resolution along the denoising trajectory from global structure formation to fine-grained detail refinement. At comparable active parameter counts, PixelMoE consistently outperforms its dense counterparts across model scales, demonstrating effective sparse capacity scaling in pixel space. On class-conditional ImageNet-1K, PixelMoE achieves FID scores of 1.47 at 256x256 and 1.53 at 512x512 without representation alignment or perceptual losses, comparing favorably with leading pixel-space and latent-space generative models. Code and models will be released soon.
authors: Ruixiao Dong, Jianmin Bao, Bozhi Luan, Zijie Meng, Xin Tao, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai, Li Li, Houqiang Li
bullets: Addresses the challenge of scaling pixel-space diffusion, where dense models tie capacity to active computation.
Uses standard Token-Choice routing, fine-grained routed experts, a shared expert, and bias-based load balancing—without diffusion-specific routing or auxiliary routing losses.
Introduces Pixel-Space Hierarchical Flow Matching to shift from global structure formation to fine-detail refinement across denoising.
At comparable active parameter counts, consistently outperforms dense counterparts across model scales.
Reports FID 1.47 at 256×256 and 1.53 at 512×512 on class-conditional ImageNet-1K, without representation alignment or perceptual losses.
papers.selection_reason: Sparse MoE scaling for pixel-space diffusion reduces active computation, relevant to efficient AI despite being image-focused.
papers.title: PixelMoE: Scaling Pixel-Space Diffusion with LLM-Style Mixture-of-Experts
papers.tldr: PixelMoE scales pixel-space diffusion efficiently by combining LLM-style sparse Mixture-of-Experts with hierarchical flow matching, achieving strong ImageNet generation quality without latent representations.

papers.abstract: Residual connections propagate information through a network by additively accumulating layer outputs. Recently proposed alternatives, such as Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) and Attention Residuals (AttnRes), instead use more expressive depth aggregation mechanisms that improve language modeling performance at scale. In this work, we consider the mixing of representations over depth as a problem of storing and retrieving information across layers. Formalizing this perspective, we introduce Depth Memory (DM), a unified framework that describes the standard pre-layer-norm (PreLN) transformer, mHC, and AttnRes in terms of streams that carry representations through the network. One such stream, for example, could be an explicit memory stream that is queried to enrich the input to every layer, and whose output is subsequently written back into the memory for use by later layers. For AttnRes, this memory stream is a growing cache of explicit layer representations. For mHC, it is an expanded residual stream. Building on this view, we propose Linear Depth Memory (LDM), which formulates information retrieval across depth as a regression problem solved using recursive least squares. The resulting architecture propagates three streams across depth: the standard residual stream, a linear associative memory stream, and an inverse covariance stream. For high-throughput training and inference, we propose a hardware-aware implementation of LDM that reduces peak activation memory and memory traffic. LDM consistently achieves the lowest perplexities among PreLN, mHC and AttnRes baselines at the 400M and 1.5B parameter scales, alongside competitive zero-shot accuracy.
authors: David Gonz\'alez-Mart\'inez, Philipp Nazari, T. Konstantin Rusch, Shiwei Liu
bullets: Frames representation mixing across layers as storing and retrieving information through depth.
Unifies PreLN Transformers, mHC, and AttnRes as stream-based memory mechanisms.
Introduces LDM, using recursive least squares to retrieve information across depth.
LDM propagates residual, associative-memory, and inverse-covariance streams.
At 400M and 1.5B parameters, LDM reports the lowest perplexities among the compared baselines and competitive zero-shot accuracy.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a unified depth-memory framework and linear associative memory stream for transformer architectures, improving language modeling and memory efficiency.
papers.title: Depth Memory
papers.tldr: Depth Memory unifies residual-style depth aggregation as information storage and retrieval, and its Linear Depth Memory variant improves language-model perplexity with hardware-efficient execution.

papers.abstract: Speculative Decoding (SD) has demonstrated its efficacy in accelerating large language model inference, but for Vision-Language Models (VLMs), the diverse input modalities make it difficult for a small trained drafter to achieve consistently high throughput. Self-speculative decoding reuses parts of the target model as a drafter which retains the multi-modal capability of the VLMs, yet its efficiency depends on choosing a suitable draft configuration for each prompt. We propose Single-Peak SPeculative decoding (SP$^2$ec), a training-free bandit algorithm that adapts the draft configuration during generation. SP$^2$ec exploits the single-peak throughput pattern observed in existing self-speculative methods, including SWIFT, KnapSpec, SpecVLM, and our simple cosSim. Our algorithmic design explicitly minimizes a novel notion of wall-time regret for each given query, corresponding to the empirical wall-time latency. Theoretical guarantees on the wall-time regret show that SP$^2$ec can exploit the optimal draft configuration, with negligible exploration cost. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B across visual and textual tasks show consistent improvements of up to 11\% over the original self-speculative methods, demonstrating the wide applicability of the proposed SP$^2$ec algorithm.
authors: Yuqi Huang, Xingyao Li, Yunlong Hou, Fengzhuo Zhang, Jiachun Pan, Vincent Y. F. Tan
bullets: VLM inputs make it difficult for a separately trained draft model to deliver consistent speculative-decoding speedups.
SP²ec reuses parts of the target VLM and adapts its draft configuration separately for each prompt during generation.
It exploits the empirically observed single-peak relationship between draft configuration and throughput.
The method minimizes query-specific wall-time regret and has theoretical guarantees with negligible exploration cost.
Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B report improvements of up to 11% over original self-speculative methods across visual and textual tasks.
papers.selection_reason: Adaptive self-speculative decoding reduces VLM inference latency; fits efficient AI though no specific subtopic matches.
papers.title: SP$^2$ec: Adaptive Self-Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models

papers.abstract: Image-token compression must reduce computation without hurting the semantics. We introduce Varest, guided by semantic fungibility: tokens within a coherent semantic region can be summarized coarsely, while object boundaries and literal text require finer distinctions. Object and text localizers guide variable-resolution merging, preserving spatial coverage and finer detail at boundaries and text. Learned [REL] registers then prune visual tokens after early decoder processing. Training across budgets enables one checkpoint per backbone. Across three backbones and 13 benchmarks, Varest outperforms 15 baselines in mean performance retention at every evaluated budget, retaining 86.10-92.33% of full-token performance with only 5.56% of the original layer-averaged image-token count.
authors: Tianhao Fu, Austin Wang, Charles Chen, Roby Aldave-Garza, Victor Xie, Xiyue Jiao, Yucheng Chen, Martin Tin
bullets: Targets lower computation without sacrificing semantic understanding.
Uses semantic, variable-resolution token merging guided by object and text localization.
Preserves spatial coverage and finer distinctions at object boundaries and literal text.
Learned [REL] registers perform additional relevance pruning after early decoder processing.
Across 3 backbones and 13 benchmarks, retains 86.10–92.33% of full-token performance using 5.56% of the original layer-averaged image tokens, outperforming 15 baselines at every evaluated budget.
