papers.selection_reason: Image-token compression via semantic merging and relevance pruning directly targets token-level efficiency for vision-language models.
papers.title: Just Respect the Semantics: Image-Token Compression via Pre-LLM Semantic Variable-Resolution Tokenization and In-LLM Relevance Pruning
papers.tldr: Varest compresses image tokens by preserving fine detail for objects and text while coarsening redundant regions, then pruning less relevant tokens inside the LLM.

papers.abstract: The Key-Value (KV) cache constitutes a dominant source of memory consumption during large language model (LLM) inference, particularly in long-context and complex reasoning scenarios. Existing KV cache quantization methods have explored different compression granularities, including layer-wise precision adjustment and token-level information preservation. In practical deployment, however, the key challenge is not merely compression, but how to allocate limited quantization resources among heterogeneous precision preservation strategies under a fixed KV cache memory budget. We propose MultiAlloc, a profiling-guided precision allocation framework for KV cache quantization that adaptively distributes limited quantization resources between layer-wise precision enhancement and token-wise preservation. MultiAlloc employs lightweight offline profiling to characterize layer sensitivity and token importance, enabling adaptive precision allocation under a fixed memory constraint. Guided by the profiled memory--accuracy trade-off, it automatically derives an effective precision allocation strategy without online allocation search, and applies the resulting policy during inference. Extensive experiments on reasoning and long-context benchmarks demonstrate that MultiAlloc consistently improves over layer-wise, token-wise, and recent multi-granularity KV cache quantization methods under matched memory budgets across diverse models, including Mistral, Llama, DeepSeek-Qwen, and QwQ.
authors: Yangchengyu Zhou, Zhiping Wu, Runchang Jiang, Dongdong Ren, Youfang Han, Wei Zhao, Dongqi Cai, Wenbin Li
bullets: Targets KV-cache memory bottlenecks in long-context and reasoning-focused LLM inference.
Profiles layer sensitivity and token importance to guide adaptive precision allocation.
Balances layer-wise precision enhancement with token-wise preservation under a fixed budget.
Derives the allocation policy offline, avoiding online allocation search.
Shows consistent gains over existing single- and multi-granularity methods across diverse models and benchmarks at matched memory budgets.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes budget-aware precision allocation for KV cache quantization, directly targeting memory-efficient LLM inference.
papers.title: MultiAlloc: Budget-Aware Precision Allocation for KV Cache Quantization
papers.tldr: MultiAlloc improves KV-cache quantization by allocating a fixed memory budget between layer- and token-level precision preservation using offline profiling.

papers.abstract: Different MRI modalities reveal different parts of a brain tumor. Segmentation models combine information from these modalities to outline tumor regions. Many models use a separate encoder for each modality. However, exchanging features among these encoders at several stages can increase model complexity. We introduce the Block-Wise Shared Adapter (BWSA), which combines compressed features from the modality encoders in a shared path and returns adapted features to each stream. In its fixed-blending form, BWSA adds the adapted features to the original features. Its trainable-gated variant (TG-BWSA) instead learns separate weights for the original and adapted features at each modality and encoder stage. We evaluate both variants on BraTS 2020 and BraTS 2023 with four segmentation backbones. On the official BraTS 2023 online validation set, BWSA increases average region-wise Dice by 1.3--7.6 percentage points relative to the corresponding unmodified backbones. TG-BWSA increases it by 2.8--7.7 points. Both variants add approximately 0.85--3.73% parameters and reduce average HD95 relative to the unmodified backbones.
authors: Milad Rostamian, Mohammadreza Mohammadi, Ender Konukoglu, Mohsen Soryani
bullets: Separate modality encoders can become complex when exchanging features across multiple stages.
BWSA compresses and combines encoder features in a shared path, then returns adapted features to each modality stream.
TG-BWSA learns stage- and modality-specific gates to balance original and adapted features.
Across four backbones on BraTS 2020/2023, both variants improve segmentation; TG-BWSA yields larger reported Dice gains on the BraTS 2023 validation set.
The adapters add approximately 0.85–3.73% parameters and reduce average HD95 versus unmodified backbones.
papers.selection_reason: Parameter-efficient shared adapters reduce trainable parameters for multimodal segmentation, fitting efficient AI.
papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Multimodal Brain Tumor Segmentation With Stage-Wise Shared Adapters
papers.tldr: BWSA and TG-BWSA enable parameter-efficient cross-modality feature sharing for multimodal brain tumor segmentation, improving Dice and HD95 with minimal added parameters.

papers.abstract: Post-training pruning enables efficient deployment, but conventional methods do not explicitly preserve internal-gradient alignment between sparse and dense models. We study novel connections between downstream performance of compressed models and the ability to retain gradient information via influence-function preservation. Central to this connection is a curvature-aware objective that accounts for both layer activations and backpropagated gradients. Despite its promise, this objective remains underexplored in pruning due to a lack of efficient solvers. We introduce $\texttt{CACTUS}$, a novel ADMM-based optimizer supporting both pruning and sparse-plus-low-rank decompositions of pre-trained weights. Compared to LLM-Surgeon which targets the same objective, $\texttt{CACTUS}$ can achieve over an order-of-magnitude speedup. At $50\%$ pruning of Qwen3-4B, $\texttt{CACTUS}$ reduces the C4 perplexity gap to the dense model by $45\%$, improves compressed-to-dense per-sample gradient cosine similarity on WikiText-2 from $0.670$ to $0.755$, and runs over $28\times$ faster than LLM-Surgeon on substantially weaker hardware. By preserving influence functions, $\texttt{CACTUS}$ supports effective data selection. On Llama-3.2-3B, fine-tuning a fresh dense model on the $5\%$ of data selected by $\texttt{CACTUS}$ achieves $49.44\%$ accuracy on BIG-Bench Hard, compared with $47.22\%$ using ALPS and $49.54\%$ using dense-model selection. Finally, integrating $\texttt{CACTUS}$ with LoGRA, a recent gradient-projection strategy, on Qwen3-4B with MLP layers pruned to 2:4 sparsity and a rank-64 correction retains a $0.711$ cosine alignment with dense LoGRA-projected C4 gradients.
authors: Mehdi Makni, Natalia Ponomareva, Rahul Mazumder
bullets: Targets the gap between efficient pruning and preservation of internal-gradient alignment with dense models.
Optimizes layer activations and backpropagated gradients through a curvature-aware objective.
Supports both pruning and sparse-plus-low-rank weight decompositions via ADMM.
At 50% Qwen3-4B pruning, it narrows the C4 perplexity gap by 45%, raises WikiText-2 gradient cosine similarity from 0.670 to 0.755, and runs over 28× faster than LLM-Surgeon on weaker hardware.
Preserved influence functions enable effective data selection; 5% CACTUS-selected data reaches 49.44% BIG-Bench Hard accuracy, close to dense-model selection at 49.54%.
papers.selection_reason: Curvature-aware post-training pruning for LLMs directly targets efficient deployment and memory/compute reduction.
papers.title: Two For The Price Of One: Curvature-Aware Pruning Preserves Influence Functions Too
papers.tldr: CACTUS uses curvature-aware ADMM optimization to prune or decompose pretrained models while better preserving gradients, influence functions, and downstream utility.

papers.abstract: Few-step distillation reduces the sampling cost of diffusion and flow models, but existing approaches often require auxiliary score models or specialized architectures. We show that simple on-policy velocity regression already provides a strong foundation for 4-NFE generation. To represent teacher velocity variation within each coarse transition, we introduce Pivot, a training-only residual proxy that separates local corrections from the student's interval-mean prediction. We further repel the student from weaker teacher predictions, providing a lightweight mechanism for avoiding undesirable modes. The resulting framework, Simplified Matching Distillation (SMD), remains entirely regression-based, requires neither online score estimation nor adversarial training, and leaves the deployed generator unchanged. We evaluate SMD on image generation and editing, 3D generation, video synthesis, and joint audio--video generation, scaling to 33 billion parameters. At 4-NFE, SMD outperforms strong few-step baselines and surpasses multi-step teachers on several benchmarks. It also supports cross-model, multi-teacher, and causal-video distillation.
authors: Jiawei Zhang, Ziyu Wan, Nanye Ma, Long Zhao, Dong Chen, Hongyu Liu, Qifeng Chen, Dongdong Chen
bullets: Uses on-policy velocity regression as the foundation for few-step distillation.
Introduces Pivot, a training-only residual proxy that captures teacher velocity variation within coarse transitions.
Repels the student from weaker teacher predictions to reduce undesirable modes.
Evaluated across image, 3D, video, and joint audio–video generation, including models up to 33B parameters.
Supports cross-model, multi-teacher, and causal-video distillation; reports outperforming strong few-step baselines and surpassing multi-step teachers on several benchmarks.
papers.selection_reason: Few-step diffusion distillation reduces sampling cost and is evaluated on video synthesis, fitting video diffusion and efficient inference.
papers.title: Simplifying and Improving On-Policy Distillation for Few-Step Diffusion
papers.tldr: SMD simplifies few-step diffusion distillation into a regression-based method that achieves strong 4-NFE generation without auxiliary score models or deployment-time architecture changes.

papers.abstract: Visual token pruning for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) appears highly effective, with existing methods retaining over 95% of unpruned performance on common VQA benchmarks using a quarter of the visual tokens or fewer. However, our extensive evaluation of ten methods across three MLLM families and five ability groups reveals a critical gap: strong general performance often comes at the cost of severe degradation on fine-grained tasks such as OCR and visual grounding. We trace these failures to two limitations of the prevailing paradigm of retaining the highest-ranked native patches. A single importance ranking overlooks the complementary evidence required by different tasks, while sparse patch selection disrupts both image content and spatial integrity. To address these limitations, we propose Bifocal, a training-free, two-stage pruning method built on a mixed-granularity framework. It allocates separate budgets to query-focused and image-intrinsic evidence, complemented by a pooled coarse representation of the entire image. Before the LLM, Bifocal matches question words to visual regions through a soft conjunction balanced against norm-debiased image saliency, while selecting image-intrinsic evidence to maximize representational coverage. Inside the LLM, it further prunes tokens using density-adjusted text-to-image attention. With roughly a quarter of the original visual tokens, Bifocal is the only evaluated method to retain over 90% of unpruned performance in every ability group across all three models, and ranks first on average in all nine model-budget settings. The code is available at: https://github.com/EIT-NLP/Bifocal
authors: Peiran Yin, Hao Wu, Zihao Yang, Fengyu Zhou, Yijuan Liang, Haozhe Hu, Xudong Wang, Wei Zhang, Xiaoyu Shen
bullets: Existing pruning methods can retain strong overall performance but substantially harm OCR and visual grounding.
Bifocal uses mixed-granularity pruning with separate query-focused and image-intrinsic token budgets plus a pooled whole-image representation.
It matches question words to regions, balances this with norm-debiased image saliency, maximizes coverage, and applies density-adjusted text-to-image attention pruning inside the LLM.
Using roughly one-quarter of the visual tokens, it retained over 90% of unpruned performance in every evaluated ability group across three MLLM families.
The method was evaluated across ten pruning methods, five ability groups, and nine model-budget settings; code is publicly available.
papers.selection_reason: Training-free visual token pruning for MLLMs, directly relevant to efficiency and multimodal foundation models.
papers.title: Bifocal: Training-Free Mixed Granularity Visual Token Pruning for Multimodal LLMs
papers.tldr: Bifocal is a training-free visual-token pruning method that preserves fine-grained and general MLLM abilities by combining query-focused, image-intrinsic, and coarse image evidence.

papers.abstract: Equivariant machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) promise atomistic simulations with accuracy approaching that of quantum-mechanical calculations. However, the high computational cost of their core Clebsch--Gordan tensor product (CGTP) convolutions severely limits model scalability and efficiency. In this paper, we rethink the parallel execution of CGTP convolutions and introduce LunaTP. Built on node-centric execution, LunaTP exploits path-group parallelism and multi-level reuse to accelerate CGTP convolutions and higher-order derivative computation while preserving the underlying mathematical formulation. On an NVIDIA H100 GPU, LunaTP achieves kernel speedups of up to 250.0$\times$ over e3nn and 17.1$\times$ over OpenEquivariance. It also delivers end-to-end training throughput gains of up to 28.7$\times$ over e3nn and 3.11$\times$ over OpenEquivariance. Finally, LunaTP demonstrates scalability and robust performance across models, workload scales, and GPUs, delivering substantial acceleration for training and atomistic simulation with high-accuracy equivariant MLIPs.
authors: Yuanchang Zhou, Mingzhen Li, Chen Wang, Xiangyu Zhang, Guangming Tan, Weile Jia
bullets: Targets the high computational cost that limits the scalability of equivariant machine-learning interatomic potentials.
Uses node-centric execution, path-group parallelism, and multi-level reuse to speed convolutions and higher-order derivatives.
Reports kernel speedups of up to 250.0× over e3nn and 17.1× over OpenEquivariance on an NVIDIA H100 GPU.
Achieves end-to-end training throughput gains of up to 28.7× over e3nn and 3.11× over OpenEquivariance.
Shows robust performance across models, workload scales, and GPUs, supporting faster training and atomistic simulation.
papers.selection_reason: GPU kernel acceleration for equivariant tensor products directly targets efficient AI computation and training throughput for equivariant MLIPs.
papers.title: LunaTP: Enabling Efficient and Scalable Tensor Product for Equivariant MLIPs
papers.tldr: LunaTP substantially accelerates Clebsch–Gordan tensor-product convolutions in equivariant MLIPs while preserving their mathematical formulation.

papers.abstract: Post-training quantisation reduces the memory cost of large language models, but it remains unclear whether compression preserves language skills of regional varieties as reliably as their standard-language counterparts. We study this question for Bavarian, Standard German, and English using BAVGROUND, a multiple-choice benchmark, where 206 source questions are aligned across all three languages. Across 14 open-weight 7B--10B instruction models, we compare BF16 with 8-bit GPTQ and two 4-bit settings, GPTQ and AWQ. Eight-bit GPTQ remains close to BF16 and largely preserves the relative behaviour of the three languages, while 4-bit quantisation was found to be much less stable. The two 4-bit methods reduce average accuracy by about 1.4--1.5 percentage points and change 11.9--16.0% of BF16 decisions, with changes concentrated on examples where the BF16 model is already uncertain. This instability does not translate into a consistent Bavarian disadvantage. Although Bavarian, a low-resource dialect, has lower baseline accuracy than German and English, the language most affected at 4 bits varies across models and quantisation methods. Calibration further shapes these cross-language effects: the relative Bavarian--German effect changes with calibration language, while changing the calibration source has little average effect on GPTQ-4 but can affect AWQ-4 much more strongly. Free-form evaluation on five models further shows that 4-bit compression can degrade generated responses even in settings where multiple-choice accuracy changes only modestly, while 8-bit GPTQ remains comparatively stable. Overall, our results show that quantisation robustness for regional language varieties depends on the model, quantisation method, calibration data, and evaluation setting, and cannot be measured by aggregate multilingual accuracy alone.
authors: Jophin John, Michael Hoffmann, Piroska Lendvai, Florent Dufour
bullets: Evaluates Bavarian, Standard German, and English with 14 open-weight 7B–10B instruction models on 206 aligned BAVGROUND questions.
8-bit GPTQ stays close to BF16 and mostly preserves the languages’ relative performance.
GPTQ-4 and AWQ-4 lower average accuracy by about 1.4–1.5 percentage points and alter 11.9–16.0% of BF16 decisions, mainly on uncertain examples.
4-bit compression does not consistently disadvantage Bavarian; the most affected language varies by model and quantisation method.
Free-form tests show greater 4-bit degradation than multiple-choice accuracy alone suggests, while calibration language particularly affects some AWQ-4 results.
papers.selection_reason: Studies post-training quantisation of LLMs, a memory-efficiency technique, with cross-language robustness analysis.
papers.title: Lightweight but Linguistically Fair? Quantisation Robustness across Bavarian, German, and English
papers.tldr: 8-bit quantisation largely preserves multilingual and dialect performance, but 4-bit methods are unstable and can degrade outputs in model-, calibration-, and evaluation-dependent ways.

papers.abstract: Random features provide a standard approach to scaling kernel methods to large datasets by approximating the kernel with a finite-dimensional feature map. Existing works of random feature methods primarily focus on well-specified models and light-tailed noise conditions, leaving a gap in understanding their performance under more general conditions, such as misspecified models and heavy-tailed noise. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive and improved analysis of kernel ridge regression with random features (KRR-RF) under general conditions. In the light-tailed noise setting, we improve upon the worst-case uniform bounds of the feature map used in the previous works and lead to the minimax optimal learning rates with $2r+\gamma>\alpha_0$, where $(r,\gamma,\alpha_0)$ denote the regularity of the target function, the effective dimension of the kernel, and the embedding index of the RKHS, respectively. In the heavy-tailed noise setting, we leverage a recently developed Hilbert-valued Fuk-Nagaev inequality and extend the same optimal results under finite weak moment conditions. The additional cost to achieve robustness is a mildly stronger explicit sample-size requirement than in the light-tailed case. For both settings, our results recover the conditions random features budgets (up to log factors) required in the previous works. In the most benign case when $\alpha_0=\gamma$, KRR-RF are minimax optimal for all $r \in (0,1]$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to establish optimal learning rates for KRR-RF under weak moment conditions in the misspecified setting. Numerical experiments and a real data analysis validate the derived learning rates and demonstrate their practical relevance in the presence of mis-specification and heavy-tailed noise.
bullets: Addresses gaps in random-feature theory beyond well-specified models and light-tailed noise.
Improves light-tailed analysis and establishes optimal rates when 2r+γ>α₀.
Uses a Hilbert-valued Fuk–Nagaev inequality to extend guarantees to finite weak-moment noise.
Robust learning requires only a mildly stronger explicit sample-size condition than the light-tailed case.
Experiments and real-data analysis support the theoretical rates under misspecification and heavy-tailed noise.
papers.selection_reason: Random features are a standard technique for scaling kernel methods, and the paper's optimality analysis is relevant to efficient AI computation.
papers.title: On the Optimality of Random Features under General Conditions: Misspecified Cases and Robust Learning
papers.tldr: This paper proves that kernel ridge regression with random features can achieve minimax-optimal learning rates even with model misspecification and heavy-tailed noise, under suitable regularity and sample-size conditions.

papers.abstract: Guardrail approaches that rely on reasoning-based large language models (LLM) improve safety decisions, but come with substantial inference overhead due to the explicit reasoning. We introduce LR-Guard (Latent Reasoning Guardrail), an efficient and explainable guardrail that jointly learns structured latent reasoning and on-demand reasoning reconstruction. Our method distills a frozen teacher's analysis of safe and unsafe prompt interpretations and their comparison into compact latent representations. Joint training optimizes these representations for both safety prediction and reconstruction of the teacher's explicit reasoning traces, enabling human-readable explanations without requiring intermediate text generation for every decision. Experiments show that LR-Guard outperforms its explicit-reasoning teacher in most in-domain and out-of-domain settings on safety classification and explanation extraction, while achieving a 19.4x inference speedup at batch size one. Further, reconstructed reasoning traces from the latent information exhibit high semantic similarity to the teacher's explicit reasoning.
authors: Md Asiful Islam, Fahmida Alam, Mihai Surdeanu
bullets: Addresses the inference overhead of reasoning-based LLM guardrails.
Distills a frozen teacher’s safe/unsafe interpretations and comparisons into compact latent representations.
Jointly trains latent representations for safety prediction and on-demand reconstruction of human-readable reasoning traces.
Outperforms its explicit-reasoning teacher in most reported in-domain and out-of-domain safety classification and explanation-extraction settings.
Achieves a 19.4× inference speedup at batch size one, with reconstructed traces showing high semantic similarity to the teacher’s reasoning.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces LR-Guard, an efficient safety guardrail that achieves 19.4x inference speedup via latent reasoning and reconstruction, fitting both efficiency and LLM safety domains.
papers.title: Efficient Safety Guardrails through Latent Dual-Hypothesis Reasoning with On-Demand Trace Reconstruction
papers.tldr: LR-Guard delivers fast, explainable safety guardrails by replacing routine explicit reasoning with structured latent reasoning and reconstructing explanations only when needed.

papers.abstract: Benchmarks are essential for evaluating and improving large language models (LLMs). Yet many widely used benchmarks are redundant, making evaluation unnecessarily expensive. Benchmark compression lowers this cost by estimating full-benchmark scores and rankings from a partial evaluation. Research in this area has grown rapidly since 2024, but to our knowledge no survey has systematically organized its methods and findings. We review 119 papers to explain how methods choose what to evaluate, recover full-benchmark results, and verify their reliability. From this analysis, we develop a taxonomy covering compression within individual benchmarks, across benchmark suites, and during adaptive evaluation, together with work on redundancy and reliability. We compare their information needs, total costs, reliability checks, and limitations. Methods reduce evaluation costs by selecting representative subsets, using cheaper or reusable information, and testing adaptively, but risk poor coverage, inaccurate estimates, and sequential delays. The resulting taxonomy and practical guide help researchers choose, validate, and deploy methods for more efficient and reliable LLM evaluation.
authors: Guoming Ling, Yupei Lin, Zhongzhan Huang, Junxin Li, Junjie Liu, Shanshan Zhong, Hefeng Wu, Liang Lin
bullets: Identifies redundancy in widely used LLM benchmarks as a major source of unnecessary evaluation expense.
Taxonomizes methods for compression within benchmarks, across benchmark suites, and through adaptive evaluation.
Analyzes how methods select evaluations, reconstruct full-benchmark scores and rankings, and verify reliability.
Finds that representative subsets, cheaper or reusable information, and adaptive testing can reduce costs.
Highlights risks including poor coverage, inaccurate estimates, and delays from sequential evaluation, and offers practical guidance for method selection and validation.
papers.selection_reason: Survey of benchmark compression to reduce LLM evaluation cost, fitting the broad efficient-AI interest.
papers.title: Are We Testing Too Much? A Survey of Benchmark Compression for Efficient Evaluation of Large Language Models
papers.tldr: A survey of 119 papers organizes benchmark-compression methods that reduce LLM evaluation costs while highlighting their reliability and coverage risks.

papers.abstract: Prefix reuse improves LLM inference by sharing the KV cache of common prompt prefixes. This helps only if the scheduler can execute a matched branch in the current worker round. Schedulers assume that a matched prefix is ready, which holds for full attention but fails for hybrid LLMs. There, a branch (the consumer) may need recurrent state that another branch (the producer) is still computing in the same round. The native scheduler stops its waiting-queue scan at this blocked consumer, and the resulting head-of-line blocking creates \emph{execution bubbles}: idle batch slots that independent work could fill. We introduce RadixFlow, which decouples prefix matching from state readiness. Its state-ready traversal turns a global scan barrier into a local wait: only the consumer is blocked until the next round, while feasible independent branches keep filling the batch under the native state check. On five hybrid models, RadixFlow lowers mean latency by 3\% to 24\% and worker rounds by 11\% to 44\% at almost unchanged reuse. On the larger Qwen3.5 models, ablations show that most of the gain comes from traversal, which adds little on a full-attention control. Heavier rounds limit how much of this saving reaches latency.
authors: Huihao Jing, Wenbin Hu, Shaojin Chen, Haochen Shi, Haoyu Huang, Sirui Zhang, Yuxuan Liu, Zhongwei Xie, Haoran Li
bullets: Prefix matching can fail when a hybrid-LLM consumer depends on state still being computed by a producer in the same round.
The native scheduler stops scanning at the blocked consumer, causing head-of-line blocking and idle batch slots.
RadixFlow decouples prefix matching from state readiness through state-ready traversal, turning a global scan barrier into a local wait.
Across five hybrid models, it reduces mean latency by 3%–24% and worker rounds by 11%–44% with nearly unchanged prefix reuse.
Traversal provides most gains on larger Qwen3.5 models; heavier rounds limit latency improvements, while full-attention workloads see little added benefit.
papers.selection_reason: Prefix-cached hybrid LLM serving with KV cache/recurrent state scheduling; fits memory-efficient inference.
papers.title: RadixFlow: Filling Execution Bubbles in Prefix-Cached Hybrid LLM Serving
papers.tldr: RadixFlow reduces execution bubbles in prefix-cached hybrid LLM serving by letting independent requests run while blocked consumers await recurrent state.

papers.abstract: Running large language models (LLMs) on consumer hardware is bottlenecked by the key-value (KV) cache, which grows with every decoded token and quickly exhausts the memory and bandwidth of a single consumer GPU. We present SparPR (Sparse Partial Recomputation), a runtime KV-cache recovery mechanism that does not modify model weights and requires no offline training. SparPR couples three online decisions: Query-Aware key-block selection scores historical blocks against the current query; dynamic budget control estimates per-block copy and recompute costs to decide how many blocks to retain; and on-demand local recomputation with cost-aware fallback merges retained blocks into continuous spans and switches between sparse recomputation and full recovery according to a runtime cost comparison. Implemented on FlexGen/FlexLLMGen, SparPR is evaluated on a single consumer laptop (RTX 3070 Ti 8GB, Ryzen 9 6900HX, 16GB RAM). It cuts end-to-end latency by 31%, 52%, and 63% at 1k, 2k, and 4k prompt tokens respectively, with 1.4x-2.7x higher throughput, and completes an 8k-token workload in 44 minutes where the FlexGen baseline times out. Under a fixed cache budget, SparPR retains a Needle Accuracy that stays well above StreamingLLM and H2O at every keep ratio, and ablation studies confirm that the three mechanisms act jointly.
authors: Jieyun Deng, Keming Hu, Yanghe Liu, Li Feng
bullets: Targets KV-cache growth that can exhaust single consumer GPUs during long-context decoding.
Combines query-aware key-block selection, dynamic retention budgets, and cost-aware local or full recomputation.
Requires no model-weight changes or offline training and integrates with FlexGen/FlexLLMGen.
On an RTX 3070 Ti laptop, it reduces latency by 31%–63% across 1k–4k prompts and achieves 1.4×–2.7× higher throughput.
Completes an 8k-token workload in 44 minutes, while the FlexGen baseline times out; cache retention remains strong across keep ratios.
papers.selection_reason: Runtime KV-cache recovery for memory-constrained LLM inference, directly fitting efficient AI and KV-cache memory efficiency.
papers.title: SparPR: Runtime KV-Cache Recovery for Resource-Constrained LLM Inference on Consumer Hardware
papers.tldr: SparPR reduces KV-cache memory and bandwidth bottlenecks for consumer-device LLM inference through runtime, training-free partial cache recovery.

papers.abstract: Training-free diffusion-based compression methods repurpose the generative priors of a diffusion or a flow model to compress data without retraining them as task-specific codecs. Recent codebook-based approaches such as Turbo-DDCM achieve strong perceptual quality at ultra-low bitrates, but their reliance on dense Gaussian codebooks remains costly in both memory and computation, and scales poorly with the large latent dimensions of modern image and video generators. Their combinatorial bitstream encoding further becomes computationally heavy at this scale. We introduce H-DDCM, a scalable generative compression framework that replaces Gaussian codebooks with implicit randomized Hadamard dictionaries. The fast Walsh-Hadamard transform allows for implicitly synthesizing full-dimensional dictionaries with $O(d \log d)$ compute for projection and reconstruction and $O(d)$ memory, without materializing the full-dimensional dictionary. We further introduce an efficient table-free lexicographic coding scheme that makes combinatorial encoding practical at larger dimensions. Beyond images, we adapt the framework to an autoregressive video flow model and develop a streaming compression scheme that periodically re-encodes recently reconstructed frames into a fresh KV-cache prefix, preserving temporal context across segments at no additional transmitted bits. This enables long-form, close to real-time generative video compression on a single GPU. Across image and video benchmarks, H-DDCM achieves competitive rate-distortion-perception performance while substantially reducing the memory and computational overhead of codebook-based training-free generative compression.
authors: Or Ronai, Vladimir Kulikov, Tomer Michaeli
bullets: Targets the memory, computation, and encoding costs of codebook-based generative compression at large latent dimensions.
Uses randomized Hadamard dictionaries with fast Walsh-Hadamard transforms, requiring O(d log d) projection/reconstruction compute and O(d) memory.
Introduces table-free lexicographic coding to make combinatorial bitstream encoding practical at larger dimensions.
Extends the framework to autoregressive video with streaming re-encoding of reconstructed frames to preserve temporal context without extra transmitted bits.
Reports competitive rate-distortion-perception performance with substantially lower codebook-related overhead, including long-form near-real-time video compression on a single GPU.
papers.selection_reason: Reduces memory and compute of codebook-based generative compression with Hadamard dictionaries and efficient encoding.
papers.title: H-DDCM: Hadamard Codebooks for Fast Generative Image and Video Compression
papers.tldr: H-DDCM makes training-free diffusion/flow-based image and video compression scalable by replacing dense Gaussian codebooks with implicit Hadamard dictionaries and efficient coding.

papers.abstract: Vision Transformers achieve strong performance but incur high computational costs from quadratic token interactions. Training-free token reduction methods improve efficiency, but their robustness remains underexplored. We propose Prune-and Merge ViT, a training-free framework for off-the-shelf models. It combines class attention-based pruning with similarity-based merging to reduce redundancy while preserving semantic information. To evaluate robustness we introduce two metrics. Relative Accuracy Drop (RAD) measures relative accuracy degradation under transformations, and Prediction Flip Rate (PFR) quantifies prediction consistency. On pretrained ViT and DeiT, Prune-and-Merge reduces computation competitively while maintaining robustness and better accuracy than existing token reduction methods. Our analysis suggests that hybrid token reduction does not introduce hallucination-like behavior and preserves prediction stability for common image transformations.
authors: Vatsal, Soumil Malhotra, Priyanshu Chahal, Sanjeev Kumar
bullets: Addresses the quadratic cost of token interactions and limited understanding of robustness in training-free token reduction.
Uses class-attention pruning to remove less-important tokens and similarity-based merging to reduce redundancy.
Introduces Relative Accuracy Drop (RAD) and Prediction Flip Rate (PFR) to assess robustness under image transformations.
Evaluated on pretrained ViT and DeiT models, it achieves competitive compute reduction with better accuracy than existing token-reduction methods.
Finds that hybrid token reduction preserves prediction stability and does not produce hallucination-like behavior for common transformations.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes training-free token pruning and merging for Vision Transformers, directly matching token pruning and eviction.
papers.title: Scaling Vision Transformers Without Training: Prune-and-Merge Token Compression
papers.tldr: A training-free prune-and-merge strategy compresses Vision Transformer tokens while reducing computation and preserving accuracy and prediction stability.

papers.abstract: Some observation-window-based KV cache compressors use prompt attention to identify important tokens but allocate uniform or predefined budgets across heads, overlooking input-dependent differences in budget demand. We propose ChampionKV, an input-adaptive head-wise budget allocator for long-context KV cache compression. It uses the maximum aggregated observation-window attention score as a lightweight empirical proxy for attention concentration, assigning larger budgets to heads with dispersed attention and smaller budgets to concentrated heads. An abnormal-head mask and a floor-budget mechanism improve robustness under weak attention responses. ChampionKV plugs into compressors such as SnapKV and PyramidKV without changing their token-selection procedures. On LongBench and RULER, both Champion variants consistently improve over their SnapKV and PyramidKV base compressors; the improvements are largest and statistically significant on Llama3.1-70B-Instruct, especially under tight budgets, whereas results on the tested 7B/8B models remain competitive but mixed. ChampionKV does not uniformly outperform Ada-KV, whose global cross-head Top-K selection retains an advantage in several settings. Controlled analysis further shows improved retained attention mass over the corresponding base compressors at negligible overhead.
authors: Yuechuan Chen, Yanda Guo, Xiaoxi Liu, Weilin Ruan, Huanbo Xu, Ruyi Wang, Wei Zhu
bullets: Addresses uniform or predefined per-head budgets that overlook input-dependent differences in attention demand.
Uses maximum aggregated observation-window attention as a proxy: dispersed heads receive larger budgets, while concentrated heads receive smaller ones.
Adds abnormal-head masking and a floor budget to improve robustness under weak attention responses.
Integrates with SnapKV and PyramidKV without changing their token-selection procedures.
Improves retained attention mass with negligible overhead, but does not consistently surpass Ada-KV; gains are mixed on tested 7B/8B models.
papers.selection_reason: Directly addresses KV cache compression with input-adaptive head-wise budget allocation, fitting the KV cache and memory efficiency subtopic.
papers.title: ChampionKV: Head-Wise Adaptive Budget Allocation for KV Cache Compression
papers.tldr: ChampionKV adaptively allocates KV-cache budgets across attention heads using attention concentration, improving long-context compression—especially for Llama3.1-70B-Instruct and tight budgets.

papers.abstract: Non-prefix KV cache reuse is a promising approach for improving inference efficiency in multi-agent systems as agents share the same context blocks. However, when agents have conflicting tasks, directly reusing non-prefix KV caches across agents can severely degrade model performance, causing up to a 90% drop. Existing remedies, including selective recomputation and offset-based calibration, recover a limited fraction of this loss. We argue that the problem lies not only in contaminated KV representations but also in the agent's difficulty interpreting reused context under its own instructions. To this end, we introduce LatentRemedy, which uses a few task-conditioned latent tokens to help the target agent leverage reused context without recomputing the shared block. Specifically, we use an MLP to map the last hidden state of the target prefix into a small number of latent tokens, which are placed after the reused KV block to interact with the shared context. To guide subsequent predictions toward the target task, we train the MLP through full-prefill distillation. Experiments show that LatentRemedy consistently outperforms existing reuse baselines on conflicting tasks while maintaining TTFT close to direct reuse as cache size grows. Code and data are available at https://github.com/chenzhwsysu57/kvreuse.
authors: Zhiwei Chen, Zhongtao Rao, Waikit Xiu, Yuxiang Zhang, Shuting Cui, Jian Chen, Tianxiang Zhao
bullets: Non-prefix KV reuse improves inference efficiency but can cause up to a 90% performance drop when agents have conflicting tasks.
The method maps the target agent’s final prefix hidden state to a small set of latent tokens using an MLP.
These tokens are inserted after the reused KV block to help the target agent interpret shared context under its own instructions.
Full-prefill distillation trains the MLP to guide predictions toward the target task.
LatentRemedy consistently outperforms existing reuse remedies while keeping TTFT close to direct reuse as cache size increases.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces task-conditioned latent tokens to remedy non-prefix KV cache reuse, improving inference efficiency in multi-agent LLM systems.
papers.title: LatentRemedy: Efficient Remedy For Non-Prefix KV Cache Reuse in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.tldr: LatentRemedy restores performance in non-prefix KV cache reuse for conflicting multi-agent tasks by adding a few task-conditioned latent tokens instead of recomputing shared context.

papers.abstract: Long-running agents retain KV caches across turns and sessions for hours or days. Compressing these persistent caches requires reducing storage while controlling reconstruction error. We present AlignPred, a codec that combines local alignment with predictive coding under a configurable KV reconstruction-error budget. Local orthogonal transforms align related heads or layers into a common coordinate frame, allowing AlignPred to combine token-wise prediction with same-token prediction across heads or layers. Residuals are quantized on an error-bounded lattice and entropy-coded, without learned predictors, encoder-side mode search, or large joint transforms. Across three attention mechanisms, AlignPred requires less storage than the evaluated baselines at comparable measured reconstruction error. Against the evaluated CPU codec implementations, it decodes at least 1.6 times faster while matching or improving encode time. AlignPred achieves near-native task scores at substantially compressed operating points on LongBench-Pro at 128K context. AlignPred's SGLang HiCache integration reduces persistent target-KV storage by 42-72% relative to native HiCache, with comparable latency.
authors: Xu Yang, Jiapeng Zhang, Zhiwei Zuo, Yuxin Chen, Feiqiang Sun, Chengguang Xu, Feng Jin, Zhuo Tang
bullets: Targets long-running agents that retain KV caches across turns and sessions.
Combines local orthogonal alignment with token-wise and cross-head/layer predictive coding.
Uses error-bounded lattice quantization and entropy coding without learned predictors or large joint transforms.
Uses less storage than evaluated baselines at comparable reconstruction error and decodes at least 1.6× faster than evaluated CPU codecs.
Reduces SGLang HiCache persistent target-KV storage by 42–72% with comparable latency and near-native LongBench-Pro scores at 128K context.
papers.selection_reason: Presents an error-controlled KV cache compression codec, directly targeting memory-efficient inference.
papers.title: AlignPred: Error-Controlled KV Cache Compression via Alignment and Predictive Coding
papers.tldr: AlignPred compresses persistent KV caches with bounded reconstruction error while reducing storage and maintaining fast decoding and near-native long-context performance.

papers.abstract: Long-context inference makes the key-value (KV) cache a major memory bottleneck for large language models. We propose BELT, a low-rank KV cache compression framework. Its key-side objective targets attention distributions rather than raw keys or pre-softmax logits, yielding a quadratic surrogate with a closed-form low-rank solution. A learned global rank allocator uses differentiable soft selection during training and hard selection at deployment to meet a user-specified component budget. Experiments demonstrate improved model quality under aggressive compression and increased decoding throughput at comparable accuracy. Evaluated across three LLMs and multiple benchmarks, BELT achieves up to 70% low-rank KV cache compression while outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 23.3 points on LongBench, and up to 17.8x overall KV cache reduction when combined with quantization. With Triton-based GPU kernels and a quantized cache, BELT delivers up to 2.7x speedup for the attention module and 3.3x end-to-end decoding throughput.
authors: Yaoyang Liu, Shuwei Shen, Jincheng Tang, Jinguang Liu, Jinbao Xue, Hailong Yang, Ke Zhang, Yinjun Wu
bullets: Targets attention distributions rather than raw keys or logits, producing a quadratic objective with a closed-form low-rank solution.
Learns global top-k rank allocation using differentiable soft selection during training and hard selection at deployment.
Across three LLMs and multiple benchmarks, achieves up to 70% low-rank KV-cache compression and up to 17.8× reduction with quantization.
Reports up to 23.3-point LongBench gains over the strongest baseline and up to 3.3× end-to-end decoding throughput.
Uses Triton GPU kernels and quantized caches to reach up to 2.7× attention-module speedup.
papers.selection_reason: Low-rank KV cache compression with learned rank allocation for long-context LLM inference, directly targeting KV-cache memory efficiency.
papers.title: BELT : BEhavior-Aligned Low-Rank KV Cache Compression with Learned Top-k Rank Allocation
papers.tldr: BELT compresses long-context KV caches with behavior-aligned low-rank representations and learned rank allocation, improving memory efficiency and decoding speed while preserving quality.

papers.abstract: The design of attention mechanisms in long-context large language models faces an ``impossible triangle'' among KV cache size, training and prefill FLOPs, and model quality. GQA achieves strong quality but incurs high KV cache overhead; alternative approaches such as MLA and MFA can compress the cache, but MLA suffers from quality loss while MFA substantially increases training and prefill compute. We propose Virtual Head Attention (VHA), which simultaneously improves all three vertices through two lightweight linear operations: Q Premix applies a near-identity transformation to queries within each KV group to recover virtual head diversity from halved physical query heads, and Linear Postmix fuses inter-head features via a low-rank $I + AB^\top$ residual structure. Since VHA introduces no nonlinear operations, Premix can be folded into the query projection and Postmix into the output projection at inference time, reducing the model to a standard GQA-2 architecture that directly reuses all existing GQA inference optimizations. With only two KV heads, the group size in large models readily reaches 64, fully exploiting Tensor Core parallelism during decoding. Across four scales with 4K-context 50B-token pretraining, VHA consistently surpasses the standard GQA baseline at every scale ($+$0.05\% to $+$0.81\%), while reducing KV cache by $4\times$ vs.\ GQA-8 at dense scales and $2\times$ vs.\ GQA-4 at the MoE scale, and lowering training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9\% (1.7B, $S{=}4096$). On an industrial 30B-A3B MoE model trained on 500B tokens at 8K context, VHA outperforms both MLA and GQA-4 by $+$0.70\,/\,$+$2.60\,\% on a 12-benchmark base-model evaluation suite; in a separate matched 10B-A1B MoE comparison after long-context mid-training, VHA attains an average RULER score of 84.4 over 8K--128K versus 73.0 for GQA, while using two rather than four KV heads in the full-attention layers.
authors: Xibo Ding, Guoxia Wang, Jinle Zeng, Jiabin Yang, Sirui Tao, Chao Yang, Dianhai Yu
bullets: Targets the trade-off among KV-cache size, training/prefill compute, and model quality in long-context LLMs.
Uses two lightweight linear operations: Q Premix restores virtual query-head diversity, while Linear Postmix fuses inter-head features with a low-rank residual structure.
The operations can be folded into existing projections at inference, yielding a standard GQA-2 model compatible with GQA optimizations and Tensor Core decoding.
Across four model scales, VHA improves over GQA while reducing KV cache by 2–4× and training/prefill FLOPs by 7.9% in one reported setting.
On industrial MoE evaluations, VHA outperforms MLA and GQA and achieves higher long-context RULER scores than GQA while using fewer KV heads.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a linear attention variant that reduces KV cache size and training/prefill FLOPs for long-context LLMs, directly advancing efficient attention and KV-cache efficiency.
papers.title: Virtual Head Attention
papers.tldr: Virtual Head Attention (VHA) reduces KV-cache and compute costs while maintaining or improving long-context language-model quality over standard attention alternatives.

papers.abstract: Traditional time-series classification methods often operate as black boxes, providing a class prediction without indicating which time point or time interval within the series led to that prediction. To improve temporal interpretability, MILLET (Multiple Instance Learning with Temporal Explanation), which combines an InceptionTime encoder with Conjunctive Pooling, provides both classification and temporal explanations. However, MILLET contains approximately 424 K parameters, making it unsuitable for deployment on resource-constrained micro-controllers, and it achieves an overall time-series accuracy of 0.888 and an explanation score of 0.681 NDCG@n. We therefore propose SEA-Net, a lightweight architecture using small multi-scale depthwise-separable convolutional TSC encoders and improved Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) pooling heads. Our SEA-Net bottleneck encoder with Top-k pooling achieves 0.931 accuracy and 0.765 NDCG@n with only 41 K parameters. Another variant, using a gated encoder with Top-k pooling, achieves 0.955 accuracy and 0.750 NDCG@n with 62 K parameters. These results demonstrate that lightweight architectures can maintain strong classification performance and temporal explanations while substantially reducing model size. The proposed variants address specific limitations of the pooling strategy used by MILLET, providing a practical direction for interpretable time-series classification on resource-constrained edge devices.
bullets: Addresses black-box time-series classifiers that do not identify influential time points or intervals.
Uses small multi-scale depthwise-separable convolutional encoders with improved multiple-instance-learning pooling heads.
The bottleneck encoder with Top-k pooling achieves 0.931 accuracy and 0.765 NDCG@n using 41K parameters.
The gated encoder with Top-k pooling achieves 0.955 accuracy and 0.750 NDCG@n using 62K parameters.
Targets practical deployment on microcontrollers and edge devices while preserving temporal interpretability.
papers.selection_reason: Lightweight interpretable time-series architecture for resource-constrained deployment; relevant to Efficient AI.
papers.title: Sea-Net: A Small and Inherently Interpretable Neural Network for Time Series Classification
papers.tldr: SEA-Net delivers interpretable time-series classification on resource-constrained devices with far fewer parameters than MILLET while achieving strong accuracy and temporal explanation quality.

papers.abstract: As generative language models become more capable and widely used, inference demand grows, making efficient serving increasingly important. Discrete diffusion language models (dLLMs) offer a promising path to more efficient inference through parallel token generation. Prior dLLM decoding methods, however, focus on improving inference efficiency for individual sequences. We formulate fixed-budget dLLM batch decoding and introduce Batch-Paced, a training-free method that jointly optimizes the allocation of decoding compute across requests to improve overall batch quality. Across two dLLM backbones, five benchmarks and their representative mixtures, Batch-Paced improves batch performance under matched budgets; gains generally grow with batch size and largely persist across decoding configurations. Analysis of requests' decoding trajectories suggests that these gains arise largely by raising the committed-token confidence of lower-confidence requests. We further show that Batch-Paced's batch decode time remains competitive and that adding a decoding-depth allowance during Batch-Paced decoding can shorten it further at a modest performance cost.
authors: Shuai Zhang, Zhanchao Zhou, Huachuan Qiu, Anqi Li, Zhenzhong Lan
bullets: Targets inefficient batch serving when inference compute is limited.
Introduces a training-free scheduler that jointly allocates decoding effort across requests.
Improves batch performance across two dLLM backbones, five benchmarks, and representative mixtures under matched budgets.
Benefits generally increase with batch size and persist across decoding configurations.
Maintains competitive batch decode time; limiting decoding depth can reduce latency with modest performance cost.
papers.selection_reason: Fixed-budget batch decoding for discrete diffusion language models targets inference efficiency and compute allocation, fitting the efficient-AI theme.
papers.title: Batch-Paced: Fixed-Budget Batch Decoding in Discrete Diffusion Language Models
papers.tldr: Batch-Paced improves fixed-budget batch decoding for discrete diffusion language models by allocating compute across requests rather than decoding each sequence independently.

papers.abstract: Post-hoc linearization is an attractive way to accelerate pretrained Video Diffusion Transformers (Video DiTs), yet existing methods largely treat the quality loss induced by attention replacement as a recovery problem. We show that a more fundamental bottleneck lies upstream: \emph{initialization}. Random initialization discards pretrained knowledge, whereas manual weight reuse transfers it through rigid and incomplete source--target correspondences. We introduce \textbf{LinMorph}, which recasts Video DiT linearization as a learnable softmax-to-linear weight transformation problem. Instead of copying predefined counterparts, LinMorph learns a cross-parameter morphism that lets each target Gated DeltaNet (GDN) parameter draw jointly from pretrained query, key, value, and output projections, including for parameters with no direct softmax counterpart. A single morphism is shared across layers and learned through local teacher alignment, while producing layer-specific initializations from their respective pretrained weights. The resulting weights are then materialized as independent GDN modules for progressive distillation and joint recovery.Since the morphism operates in weight space rather than token space, it can be learned on short, low-resolution clips and directly reused at larger video scales. Across pretrained Video DiTs, LinMorph enables markedly faster recovery and better final generation quality than random initialization and heuristic weight reuse. Results show that efficient linearization depends not only on how a converted model is recovered, but critically on how pretrained knowledge is transferred before recovery. Project page: https://lonelyling.github.io/LinMorph.
authors: Lingyi Long, Congyue Zhao, Xiaoou Li, Yanmin Qian, Tao Huang
bullets: Identifies initialization—not only post-conversion recovery—as a key bottleneck in Video DiT linearization.
Learns a shared cross-parameter softmax-to-linear morphism instead of relying on random initialization or rigid weight copying.
Allows each GDN parameter to combine information from pretrained query, key, value, and output projections, including unmatched parameters.
Uses local teacher alignment on short, low-resolution clips, then applies layer-specific transformed weights for progressive distillation and recovery.
Reports faster recovery and better final generation quality across pretrained Video DiTs than random or heuristic initialization.
papers.selection_reason: Presents a weight-morphing method to linearize Video Diffusion Transformers, improving efficiency of video DiT inference.
papers.title: LinMorph: Learning to Morph Weights for Efficient Video DiT Linearization
papers.tldr: LinMorph learns how to transfer pretrained attention weights into linear Gated DeltaNet modules, enabling faster Video DiT linearization with better recovered quality.

papers.abstract: Long-context training of large language and multimodal models couples structured attention masks (document, prefix-LM, share-question, sliding-window, block-sparse) with multi-node context parallelism, making the mask a dominant bottleneck. FlashMask's column-wise sparse mask compresses them from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n)$ via four query-axis boundary vectors, covering broad structured patterns. Implemented for Ampere GPUs, it neither exploits FlashAttention-3's TMA/WGMMA warp-specialized pipeline on Hopper nor supports distribution. The column-wise sparse mask is indexed by key positions but stores query-axis interval boundaries. Under any multi-chunk context-parallel assignment, it reduces per-rank mask localization to a provably zero-communication \emph{clip--shift--max} on the boundary vectors, compatible with the single-GPU kernel. FlashMask-3 introduces a mask-aware Hopper kernel with three-role warp specialization atop FlashAttention-3's TMA/WGMMA pipeline, plus a mask-aware distributed extension: zero-communication mask localization, a sparsity-aware load balancer (HCC-IPO), and a mask-aware compute-communication overlap with mask-driven communication pruning, whose forward all-gather uses topology-aware hierarchical routing. On a single H100 across 12 masks at 4K--128K context, it improves achieved TFLOPs over FlashMask, FlexAttention, and MagiAttention by 45--141%, 34--71%, and 2--44%. At context-parallel degrees 4--32 with 8K sequence per device, it attains 31--75% compute-communication overlap efficiency and improves throughput over Megatron-Core CP ring, Megatron-Core CP all-gather, and MagiAttention by $1.80\times$--$3.71\times$, $1.71\times$--$2.92\times$, and $1.09\times$--$1.46\times$. In end-to-end training of a 118B-A14B MoE at 128K on 128 H100 GPUs, it raises throughput by 7.3--11.0% over a Dual Chunk all-gather baseline, with attention forward+backward 24.5--44.9% faster.
authors: Guoxia Wang, Qianyue He, Siming Wu, Haoyang Xie, Qiwen Bao, Jinle Zeng, Jiabin Yang, Tian Wu, Dianhai Yu
bullets: Targets the bottleneck of structured attention masks in long-context, multi-node training.
Uses a Hopper-optimized FlashAttention-3 kernel with TMA/WGMMA and three-role warp specialization.
Provides zero-communication mask localization via a clip–shift–max operation, plus load balancing and mask-aware communication overlap with pruning.
On a single H100, improves achieved TFLOPs by 2–141% over prior mask-aware attention systems across 12 masks and 4K–128K contexts.
Across 4–32 context-parallel degrees, improves throughput by up to 3.71×; in 128K end-to-end MoE training, raises throughput by 7.3–11.0%.
papers.selection_reason: Mask-aware distributed attention for long-context LLM training; directly improves attention efficiency and long-context capability.
papers.title: FlashMask-3: Efficient and Expressive Mask-Aware Distributed Attention
papers.tldr: FlashMask-3 makes structured, mask-aware attention efficient on Hopper GPUs and across distributed context parallelism, delivering substantial kernel and end-to-end training speedups.

papers.abstract: Extended chain-of-thought reasoning improves problem-solving performance but increases inference cost and latency, motivating more accurate answers with shorter reasoning. We introduce PaceReasoner, a label-free test-time reinforcement learning framework that uses a model's LONG responses to improve its SHORT-mode accuracy. Both modes share a trainable policy, creating a need for reliable supervision, sufficient SHORT training samples, and continued LONG responses to guide learning. PaceReasoner combines all-response and LONG-only answer consensus through progressive, confidence-weighted supervision. A behavior reward gradually shifts from encouraging SHORT exploration to rewarding agreement with LONG answers, while a ratio controller regulates the balance between modes. Across three model backbones and four benchmarks, PaceReasoner improves average SHORT accuracy over the baselines by 7.4--13.5 percentage points, with fewer than 25 reasoning tokens per response on average. Ablations support the key components, and cross-dataset results demonstrate transfer beyond the adaptation set.
authors: Changguo Jia, Zhiyou Xiao, Xinbei Ma, Geng Chen, Weiming Zhang, Yiming Xu, Tianqi Zhao, Minghui Zhou
bullets: Addresses the inference cost and latency of extended chain-of-thought reasoning.
Uses a shared policy with label-free test-time reinforcement learning to train SHORT responses from LONG responses.
Combines all-response and LONG-only consensus with progressive, confidence-weighted supervision.
Gradually shifts rewards from encouraging SHORT exploration to matching LONG-answer guidance, while regulating the mode balance.
Across three backbones and four benchmarks, improves average SHORT accuracy by 7.4–13.5 percentage points; results transfer beyond the adaptation set.
papers.selection_reason: Label-free test-time RL to shorten LLM reasoning while preserving accuracy, directly targeting reasoning efficiency and LLM inference cost.
papers.title: PaceReasoner: Label-Free Learning to Answer Briefly from Long Reasoning
papers.tldr: PaceReasoner uses long responses as label-free guidance to improve short-answer accuracy while keeping reasoning under 25 tokens on average.

papers.abstract: Multi-agent Large Language Model (LLM) systems typically commit to a deliberation protocol before inference. A fixed protocol cannot allocate computation differently to resolved and unresolved instances, and it may mistake repeated support for independent confirmation. We study this failure as semantic false consensus: a confident group answer supported by narrow, duplicated, or correlated rationales. We introduce ECMR, an evidence-aware controller over frozen role-conditioned LLMs. At each step, ECMR summarizes answer concentration, support diversity and independence, contradictions, role behavior, verification history, and remaining budget, then selects whether to propose, challenge, verify, arbitrate, diversify, correct a role, or stop. We formulate this decision as finite-horizon budgeted control and derive sufficient conditions under which state conditioning, risk-triggered verification, and role correction improve cost-adjusted utility. Across a declared held-out evaluation of 9,000 records from MedQA, CaseHOLD, and FinQA, ECMR-Full increases pooled accuracy from 62.1% to 84.9%, reduces false-consensus rate from 40.7% to 17.0%, and raises evidence-support rate from 58.0% to 88.7%. State shuffling loses 11.7 accuracy points with only 0.7 fewer rounds, while harder traces shift from early stopping toward arbitration. ECMR-Full uses the largest token budget, yielding the strongest absolute reliability rather than uniformly superior token efficiency.
authors: Yuan Liu, Haoyue Peng, Fanliang Hu, Lei Huang, Wenli Cai
bullets: Targets fixed deliberation protocols that waste computation and can mistake duplicated or correlated support for independent confirmation.
Controls frozen, role-conditioned agents by choosing among proposing, challenging, verifying, arbitrating, diversifying, correcting roles, or stopping.
Tracks answer concentration, evidence diversity and independence, contradictions, role behavior, verification history, and remaining budget.
On 9,000 held-out records across MedQA, CaseHOLD, and FinQA, pooled accuracy rose from 62.1% to 84.9%, while false-consensus rate fell from 40.7% to 17.0%.
The full controller uses the largest token budget, achieving stronger absolute reliability but not uniformly better token efficiency.
papers.selection_reason: Evidence-aware budgeted control for multi-agent LLM reasoning, addressing reasoning reliability, false consensus, and token-budget allocation.
papers.title: ECMR: Evidence-Aware Deliberation Control for Multi-Agent LLM Reasoning
papers.tldr: ECMR adaptively controls multi-agent LLM deliberation using evidence quality and disagreement signals to reduce false consensus and improve reliability.

papers.abstract: Diffusion language models apply bidirectional attention over the whole context at every denoising step, so a longer context makes each step substantially more expensive. Sparsifying only at inference leaves the pretrained weights unchanged, so the model is never trained under the sparse pattern it runs with. We propose Prefilling-dLLM v2, which continues training a diffusion language model so that it routes with its native mask token. One mask is appended at the end of each chunk, and a learned role offset marks it as a routing slot. On every fourth layer, a query keeps a bidirectional local window and the top-K chunks scored from that mask; the other layers use a bidirectional sliding window. Starting from Dream-v0-Base-7B extended to 16K with YaRN, we compare Prefilling-dLLM v2 with bidirectional NSA, DSA, and SWA under the same layout, key budget, and dense initialization, using the same Fast-dLLM decoder. With the YaRN factor scaled to the evaluation length, Prefilling-dLLM v2 leads the other sparse methods on all three RULER tasks from 16K to 128K. Its mean accuracy at 128K is 7.4 points above NSA, the next sparse model, while DSA and SWA remain near zero. At the same length, decoding is 172x faster than with full dense attention.
authors: Qi Han, Jing Xiong, Ziyuan Zhang, Ngai Wong
bullets: Addresses the high per-step cost of bidirectional full-context attention in diffusion language models.
Adds one learned routing mask per chunk; every fourth layer selects the top-K chunks while other layers use local sliding-window attention.
Continued training aligns the model with the sparse attention pattern used at inference.
Outperforms bidirectional NSA, DSA, and SWA across three RULER tasks from 16K to 128K; at 128K, it is 7.4 accuracy points above NSA.
Achieves 172× faster decoding than dense attention at 128K, within the evaluated setup and context range.
papers.selection_reason: Learned chunk routing and sparse attention for long-context diffusion language models directly address efficient attention and long-context processing.
papers.title: Prefilling-dLLM v2: Learned Chunk Routing for Long-Context Diffusion Language Models
papers.tldr: Prefilling-dLLM v2 trains a diffusion language model to route attention through learned chunk-level mask tokens, enabling efficient long-context decoding while preserving strong retrieval performance.

papers.abstract: Multi-agent deliberation can improve recognition by criticizing and revising candidate answers, but fixed controls cannot respond to changes in disagreement or reasoning quality. We present an adaptive multi-agent controller (ADMA) that learns continuous policies for proposal, challenge, arbitration, and coordination while keeping the task model frozen. Shared trace features describe quality, agreement, and progress, while role-specific features support decentralized control during inference. One controller trained on legal and financial reasoning is transferred without policy updates to four textual and multimodal benchmarks and two successive task-model versions. With Qwen3.5 held fixed, ADMA-Full improves accuracy by 6.2-14.2 percentage points over Direct and by 2.8-3.0 points over ADMA-Fixed. Paired bootstrap ranges for the Full-Fixed comparison are positive on three tasks. Outcome decompositions show that recoveries exceed introduced errors, while process assessment records fewer false-consensus events and more supported correct outcomes. Transfer to Qwen3.6 remains task dependent, which bounds the generality of the learned policy. Median token and latency ratios are 14.3-18.7 and 7.8-16.5 relative to Direct. These results show that adaptive deliberation can improve fixed-model recognition when its task-dependent gains justify the additional computation.
authors: Yuan Liu, Haoyue Peng, Fanliang Hu, Lei Huang, Wenli Cai
bullets: Fixed deliberation controls may fail when disagreement or reasoning quality changes.
ADMA learns continuous proposal, challenge, arbitration, and coordination policies from shared and role-specific trace features.
A controller trained on legal and financial reasoning transfers without policy updates across four textual/multimodal benchmarks and two model versions.
With Qwen3.5, ADMA-Full improves accuracy by 6.2–14.2 points over Direct and 2.8–3.0 points over ADMA-Fixed; recoveries exceed introduced errors.
Transfer to Qwen3.6 is task dependent, while token and latency costs are substantially higher than Direct.
papers.selection_reason: Learns adaptive deliberation control for multi-agent LLM reasoning and explicitly manages token/latency trade-offs, fitting LLM reasoning and efficiency interests.
papers.title: Learning Adaptive Deliberation Control for Reliable Recognition with Multi-Agent Language Models
papers.tldr: ADMA adaptively controls multi-agent deliberation to improve recognition accuracy with frozen task models, but incurs substantial computation and task-dependent transfer.

papers.abstract: Edge-cloud collaboration combines the lower inference overhead and greater data locality of edge-side execution with the stronger capabilities of cloud-hosted models. However, as LLM agents increasingly operate in long-horizon scenarios, cloud participation becomes interleaved throughout execution rather than a one-shot decision for each query. Such interleaved participation introduces trajectory-level effects that remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, we introduce EC2-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating edge-cloud collaboration in long-horizon agent execution. It provides executable digital-workspace agent tasks and a unified evaluation framework covering task performance, resource usage, and privacy exposure. Using this benchmark, we empirically study diverse forms of edge-cloud collaboration. Our study reveals three findings. First, collaboration achieves a favorable balance among task performance, resource usage, and privacy exposure compared with edge-only and cloud-only execution. Second, as edge models become stronger, collaborative execution approaches cloud-only performance, and performance differences across strategies shrink, while privacy exposure remains strongly strategy-dependent. Third, stronger edge capability shifts preferred collaboration from externally controlled cloud participation and direct cloud execution toward more edge-controlled collaboration. Further analyses identify cloud-invocation decision-making and instruction following as important edge-side abilities for effective collaboration. These findings provide a systematic understanding of edge-cloud collaboration in long-horizon agent execution and insights for designing future edge agents that effectively collaborate with cloud models. Code and resources are available at https://github.com/OpenBMB/EC2-Bench.
authors: Pengcheng Huang, Zhenghao Liu, Shixin Ren, Shi Yu, Sijia Yao, Yukun Yan, Chaojun Xiao, Maosong Sun
bullets: Introduces executable digital-workspace tasks and a unified evaluation framework for task performance, resource usage, and privacy exposure.
Finds that collaboration offers a favorable trade-off across these objectives compared with edge-only and cloud-only execution.
Stronger edge models narrow the performance gap with cloud-only execution, while privacy exposure remains dependent on the collaboration strategy.
As edge capabilities improve, preferred designs shift toward more edge-controlled collaboration.
Cloud-invocation decisions and instruction following are key edge-side abilities for effective collaboration.
papers.selection_reason: Systematically studies edge-cloud collaboration for LLM agent execution, directly addressing inference overhead, resource usage, and latency trade-offs.
papers.title: Empowering Edge Agents: A Systematic Analysis of Edge-Cloud Collaboration in LLM Agent Execution
papers.tldr: EC2-Bench systematically evaluates how edge agents should collaborate with cloud models during long-horizon tasks, balancing performance, resource use, and privacy.

papers.abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) achieve strong performance by externalizing explicit reasoning traces before producing the answer, yet suffer from overthinking challenge that allocates uniformly heavy computation to queries of varying difficulty. While proprietary models mitigate this via opaque routing, open-source LRMs still lack an efficient mechanism to internalize adaptive reasoning due to both expensive training cost and limited disclosure of training recipes. In response, we introduce RPO (Root-token Policy Optimization), a framework that enables LRMs to self-determine when to reason by training only the initial root token (e.g., whether to invoke the tag) via group relative reward and group-wise advantages. By focusing on this pivotal branching point, RPO drastically reduces training overhead and VRAM usage. Across multiple model families and scales, RPO learns difficulty-aware adaptive thinking at just ~2% of the training compute of prior adaptive-reasoning methods.
authors: Taehyeon Kim, Hyunsoo Lee, Youngsoo Jang, Moontae Lee
bullets: Addresses overthinking caused by applying equally heavy reasoning to queries of different difficulty.
Optimizes only the initial root token that decides whether to invoke explicit reasoning.
Uses group-relative rewards and group-wise advantages to learn difficulty-aware routing.
Reported across multiple model families and scales, with substantially lower training overhead and VRAM use.
The abstract does not specify detailed datasets, baselines, or inference-time gains.
papers.selection_reason: Tackles adaptive reasoning in LRMs with minimal training/inference compute; directly contributes to efficient AI and large reasoning model methodology.
papers.title: Efficiently Learning To Reason or Not to Reason: Root-token Policy Optimization for Adaptive Thinking
papers.tldr: RPO trains a reasoning model to decide when to think, reducing adaptive-reasoning training compute to about 2% of prior methods.

papers.abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) often underperforms full fine-tuning. We investigate this performance gap through a tangent-space lens: factorized updates are confined to the tangent space of the current low-rank factors, leaving gradient components outside this space unexploited. An analysis of ten representative LoRA variants reveals that these residual components account for most of the gradient energy and exhibit strong spectral concentration. Motivated by this finding, we propose Dynamic Tangent LoRA (DT-LoRA), which partitions a fixed rank budget into a stable branch and a dynamic branch to capture the principal residual gradient directions. We show that these directions define the optimal update of a local quadratic model under orthogonal-complement and rank constraints. Matrix-free randomized SVD recovers them without materializing the residual gradient, while controlled write-back preserves accumulated updates and stabilizes training within the allocated rank. DT-LoRA adds no trainable parameters or inference cost over LoRA. Experiments across computer vision and natural language processing tasks demonstrate consistent improvements over LoRA and its variants. Moreover, despite being a general-purpose adaptation method, DT-LoRA outperforms task-specific approaches to open-vocabulary domain generalization for semantic segmentation, achieving state-of-the-art results. Code is available at https://github.com/Snipine/DT-LoRA.
authors: Yangming Zhang, Ling Yi, Datong Li, Jinliang Ding, Xiaojie Wang, Tiecheng Song, Zhaolong Ning
bullets: LoRA misses substantial, spectrally concentrated gradient components outside the tangent space of its low-rank factors.
DT-LoRA divides a fixed rank budget into stable and dynamic branches to capture principal residual-gradient directions.
It uses matrix-free randomized SVD and controlled write-back to identify useful directions while preserving accumulated updates and stabilizing training.
Experiments across vision and NLP show consistent gains over LoRA variants; it also achieves state-of-the-art results for open-vocabulary domain generalization in semantic segmentation.
The method is evaluated within a fixed rank budget and is designed to add no inference overhead over LoRA.
papers.selection_reason: Low-rank adaptation method improving parameter-efficient fine-tuning; fits efficient AI.
papers.title: DT-LoRA: Reaching Beyond the Tangent Space of Low-Rank Adaptation
papers.tldr: DT-LoRA improves LoRA by using residual gradient directions outside its current tangent space, yielding stronger adaptation without extra trainable parameters or inference cost.

papers.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) improves reasoning but incurs substantial autoregressive rationale cost. Continuous CoT moves intermediate computation into recurrent hidden states, yet typically uses a fixed number of updates even though the best budget varies across questions and accuracy need not improve monotonically with $K$. We introduce Dynamic K-Head, a question-conditioned, pre-rollout budget selector. It is jointly trained with the reasoner under selected budgets, using difficulty supervision based on scores assigned from the question alone. We also show that latent-update count can misrepresent end-to-end cost because a short latent rollout can shift computation into a longer explicit continuation. We therefore count latent updates, implementation-specific special tokens, and all decoded text. Instantiated with CoDI on Llama 3.2 1B and GSM8K, Dynamic K-Head reaches 54.44% exact-match accuracy at 12.03 average reasoning/output tokens, compared with 52.31% at 15.21 tokens for fixed-$K=6$ CoDI---a 2.12-point gain with 20.9% lower token cost. Across three out-of-distribution arithmetic datasets, it reduces cost by 19.3--25.7% while improving accuracy by 0.30--2.22 points. These results demonstrate that difficulty-supervised budget selection can improve both accuracy and efficiency, while stable budget selection remains a central challenge.
authors: Ying Li, Yuqi Chen, Sixuan Li, Yunfeng Cai
bullets: Fixed latent-update budgets are inefficient because question difficulty varies and accuracy may not increase monotonically with computation.
The method jointly trains a question-conditioned budget selector and reasoner using difficulty supervision derived from the question alone.
It measures end-to-end cost using latent updates, special tokens, and decoded text, rather than latent updates alone.
On GSM8K with CoDI and Llama 3.2 1B, it achieves 54.44% exact match at 12.03 average tokens versus 52.31% at 15.21 tokens for fixed K=6.
Across three out-of-distribution arithmetic datasets, it lowers cost by 19.3–25.7% while improving accuracy by 0.30–2.22 points; stable budget selection remains challenging.
papers.selection_reason: Reduces reasoning token cost via difficulty-supervised budget selection for continuous latent reasoning, fitting the efficient AI topic.
papers.title: Dynamic K-Head: Difficulty-Supervised Budget Selection for Continuous Latent Reasoning
papers.tldr: Dynamic K-Head predicts each question’s reasoning budget before rollout, improving accuracy while reducing total token cost for continuous latent reasoning.

papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) frameworks place teacher and student on the same GPUs, so per-GPU memory limits the teachers that fit. DisaggKD separates them across nodes: teacher replicas stream hidden states to the student, a KD loss over row windows and vocabulary shards equals the full-vocabulary loss in exact arithmetic without forming the full-vocabulary logits, and a prefetch ring paces producer and trainer.
